title: 嘉靖十一年進士登科錄
text:
先司馬東明府君舉嘉靖戊子浙江鄉試迄壬辰舉進士鄉試錄登科錄
敬藏天一閣自明迄今四百年矣去歲夏閣書失竊銷售於滬上各書肆
好古家爭購之逮裔孫至杭至滬控追已不及以致全書一無返璧曷勝
歎憾邑中張讓三先生先君子舊好也今夏從上海友人處得此兩
錄暨先吏部潞公府君手鈔詩藁交小子還藏閣中蓋先生於吾閣原
委最悉前薛星使刻見存書目先生實總其成故惓惓於閣書尤切今雖
僅得此三種而先生之關懷文獻與不忘先人之交情亦足見矣用記數
語以誌銘感
乙卯仲夏司馬公十一世孫玉森謹識

punctuated:
先司馬東明府君舉嘉靖戊子浙江鄉試，迄壬辰舉進士。《鄉試錄》《登科錄》敬藏天一閣，自明迄今四百年矣。去歲夏，閣書失竊，銷售於滬上各書肆，好古家爭購之。逮裔孫至杭至滬控追，已不及，以致全書一無返璧，曷勝歎憾！邑中張讓三先生，先君子舊好也。今夏，從上海友人處得此兩錄暨先吏部潞公府君手鈔詩藁，交小子還藏閣中。蓋先生於吾閣原委最悉，前薛星使刻見存書目，先生實總其成，故惓惓於閣書尤切。今雖僅得此三種，而先生之關懷文獻與不忘先人之交情，亦足見矣。用記數語，以誌銘感。
乙卯仲夏，司馬公十一世孫玉森謹識。
translation_en:
Our late honored ancestor Dongming, Vice Minister of War, passed the Zhejiang Provincial Examination in the wuzi year of Jiajing and subsequently attained the metropolitan graduate (jinshi) degree in the renchen year. The Provincial Examination Record and the Record of Metropolitan Graduates were reverently preserved in Tianyi Pavilion. Four hundred years have now passed since the Ming dynasty. Last summer, books were stolen from the Pavilion and sold through bookshops in Shanghai, where collectors of antiquities competed to buy them. By the time his descendants reached Hangzhou and Shanghai to lodge complaints and pursue their recovery, it was already too late: not a single volume was returned. How could our sorrow and regret be exhausted!

Mr. Zhang Rangsan of our county was an old friend of my late father. This summer, he obtained these two records, together with poetry drafts copied by hand by our late honored ancestor Lu, who served in the Ministry of Personnel, from a friend in Shanghai. He entrusted them to me to return to the Pavilion. Mr. Zhang knows the history of our Pavilion most thoroughly. When the envoy Xue previously had a catalogue of its surviving books printed, it was Mr. Zhang who oversaw its completion; hence his particularly deep concern for the Pavilion’s books. Although only these three works have now been recovered, they sufficiently demonstrate his care for historical writings and his enduring remembrance of his friendship with my late father. I therefore set down these few words to record my heartfelt gratitude.

Respectfully inscribed in midsummer of the yimao year by Yusen, an eleventh-generation descendant of the Vice Minister of War.

嘉靖十一年進士登科録

玉音

嘉靖十一年三月初九日，禮部尚書兼翰林院學士臣夏言等於奉天門奏，為科舉事：「會試天下舉人，取中三百二十名。本年三月十五日殿試，合請讀卷官及執事等官，少傅兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士張孚敬等五十八員。其進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二、第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。」奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

讀卷官

光禄大夫、柱國、少傅兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士張孚敬，辛巳進士。
榮禄大夫、太子太保、禮部尚書兼武英殿大學士李時，壬戌進士。
光禄大夫、柱國、太子太保、吏部尚書王瓊，甲辰進士。
translation_en:
Record of Metropolitan Graduates of the Eleventh Year of Jiajing (1532)

The Imperial Voice

On the ninth day of the third month of the eleventh year of Jiajing, your servant Xia Yan, Minister of Rites concurrently serving as Academician of the Hanlin Academy, and others submitted a memorial at Fengtian Gate concerning the civil-service examinations:

“In the Metropolitan Examination of provincial graduates from throughout the realm, 320 candidates were selected. The Palace Examination will be held on the fifteenth day of the third month this year. We accordingly request the appointment of Zhang Fujing, Junior Mentor concurrently serving as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of the Flowery Canopy, together with the others, fifty-eight officials in all, as readers of examination papers and officials performing the various attendant duties.

“The classes of metropolitan graduate status shall respectfully follow the qualifications imperially established by Emperor Taizu Gao. In the first class, three candidates are selected according to precedent: the first receives lower sixth rank, and the second and third receive principal seventh rank; they are granted the distinction ‘metropolitan graduate with honors.’ Those in the second class receive lower seventh rank and are granted ‘metropolitan graduate status.’ Those in the third class receive principal eighth rank and are granted ‘status equivalent to metropolitan graduate.’”

The imperial rescript was received: “Approved.” Reverently received.

Readers of Examination Papers

Zhang Fujing was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Mentor concurrently serving as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of the Flowery Canopy. He became a metropolitan graduate in the xinsi year.

Li Shi was Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Rites concurrently serving as Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory. He became a metropolitan graduate in the renxu year.

Wang Qiong was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Personnel. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jiachen year.

Zhai Luan, Grand Master for Aid in Governance and Minister of Rites, concurrently Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, was a metropolitan graduate of the yichou year.

Zhang Chao, Grand Master for Central Compliance and Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Academician of the Hanlin Academy, was a metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year.

Xi Chun, Academician of the Hanlin Academy, was a metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year.

Wu Hui, Academician Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy and Grand Master for Upright Service, was a metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year.

Guo Weifan, Academician Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy and Grand Master for Meritorious Service, was a metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year.

Cai Ang, Academician Expositor-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy, was a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.

Zhan Ruoshui, Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Left Vice Minister of Rites, was a metropolitan graduate of the yichou year.

三月二十日
translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Honors

On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month of the eleventh year of Jiajing (1532), the tribute scholars proceeded to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. The emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall and personally bestowed the policy question.

On the morning of the nineteenth day of the third month, the civil and military officials attended in court dress, standing in their assigned ranks. That day, the Embroidered-uniform Guard arrayed the imperial ceremonial equipment on the vermilion steps and within the vermilion courtyard. The emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall. Officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and called out the successful candidates’ names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites carried the yellow proclamation, led by drums and music, out beyond Chang’an Left Gate and posted it there. Once this was completed, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan) back to his residence with a ceremonial parasol, canopy, and retinue.

On the twentieth day of the third month…

translation_en:
…a banquet was bestowed at the Ministry of Rites. After the banquet, the graduates went to the Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the ceremonial procedures.
On the twenty-second day of the third month, the first-place graduate was granted court robes, a cap, and a belt, and the metropolitan graduates (jinshi) were granted paper currency.
On the twenty-third day of the third month, the first-place graduate led the other metropolitan graduates in submitting a memorial expressing gratitude for imperial favor.
On the twenty-fourth day of the third month, the first-place graduate led the other metropolitan graduates to the temple of Confucius, the First Teacher, to perform the vegetable-offering ceremony.
The Ministry of Rites memorialized the throne, requesting that the Ministry of Works be ordered to erect a stone stele at the Directorate of Education and inscribe the graduates’ names upon it.

孔天胤〔貫山西汾州軍籍，州學生，治詩經，字汝錫，行一，年二十八，八月十六日生〕。曾祖表，祖大褫〔巡檢〕，父麟〔儀賓〕，母〔新鄭縣君〕。具慶下，弟天民，娶王氏，繼娶王氏。山西鄉試第六名，會試第二百七十二名。

高節〔貫四川成都府綿州羅江縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字公成，行二，年四十，正月十六日生〕。曾祖子清，祖本政，父騰〔封南京刑部主事〕，母李氏〔贈安人〕，繼母王氏〔封安人〕。具慶下，兄第〔按察司副使〕，弟策、簡〔進士〕，娶王氏。四川鄉試第二十四名，會試第一百十九名。
translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the designation “metropolitan graduate with honors” (jinshi jidi).

Lin Daqin 林大欽 was registered in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, under military-and-civilian registration. A supplementary student of the county school, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Jingfu; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-two sui, born on the sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shan, his grandfather Xuan, and his father Wu; his mother was née Liu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Sun. He placed sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Kong Tianyin 孔天胤 was registered in Fenzhou, Shanxi, under military registration. A student of the subprefectural school, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Ruxi; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-eight sui, born on the sixteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Biao; his grandfather, Dachi, was a Police Chief; and his father, Lin, was a Ceremonial Escort. His mother held the title Lady of Xinzheng County. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Tianmin. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently another woman née Wang. He placed sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 272nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Jie 高節 was registered in Luojiang County, Mianzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, under civilian registration. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Gongcheng; he ranked second among his brothers and was forty sui, born on the sixteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziqing, his grandfather Benzheng, and his father Teng, who had been honorifically granted the title Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice. His mother, née Li, had been posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace; his stepmother, née Wang, had been granted the same title. His father and stepmother were living. His elder brother Di was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; his younger brothers were Ce and Jian, the latter a metropolitan graduate (jinshi). His wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 119th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Second class: eighty men, granted metropolitan graduate (jinshi) status.

Li Qidong, registered in a civilian household in Chuxiong County, Chuxiong Prefecture, Yunnan, was originally from Luling County, Jiangxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Yuanshu, ranked first in his family, and was twenty-nine years old, born on the second day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Sicun; his grandfather, Quan, held an honorary title for public benefaction; his father, Hong, was an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His wife was née Li. He placed third in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Luo was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Jingzhi, ranked seventh in his family, and was forty years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Bingwen; his grandfather was Wanxiang; and his father, Liang, had been granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of War. His mother, née Hu, had been posthumously granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren); his stepmother was née Wang. His father and stepmother were living. His elder brother was He; his younger brothers were Ji, a Secretary in the Ministry of War; Huang, a tribute scholar (gongshi); and Zhi. His wife was née Luo. He placed 103rd in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sang Qiao was registered in a civilian household in Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Zimu, ranked second in his family, and was thirty-two years old, born on the seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Hong; his grandfather was Gui; his father, Chao, held an honorary title for longevity; and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yin and Lan, and his younger brothers were Fan and Qian. His wife was née Xu. He placed third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Huang Hua 黃崋, courtesy name Xiuqing, was registered in a civilian household in Suining County, Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan. A student of the National University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twentieth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Jian was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Aid in Governance and Minister of Works at Nanjing; his grandfather Zongsi was a county magistrate, posthumously granted those same titles through successive honors. His father Ke was Grand Master for Aid in Governance and Minister of Works at Nanjing, advanced in rank to Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, and posthumously granted the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the name Jiansu. His father's former wife, née Zhang, was posthumously honored as Lady; his mother, née Nie, was honored as Grand Lady. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Qiao and Yan; his younger brothers were Feng, a student admitted by virtue of official family status, and Yue. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Yue 楊瀹, courtesy name Honggong, was registered in a civilian household in Zhuozhou, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the thirteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Chun; his grandfather was Zan; his father, Hong, was a county magistrate; and his mother was née Fan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ze, an administrative assistant, and Pei; his younger brothers were Chao, Zhen, Jing, and Mian 汅 [?]. He married a woman née Chi and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed thirty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang He 張合, courtesy name Maoguan, was registered in an official household in Yongchang Prefecture, Yunnan, and was a native of Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zong; his grandfather Bing was posthumously granted the title Director of a Bureau in the Ministry of Personnel; and his father Zhichun was retired Right Vice Minister of Revenue at Nanjing. His legal mother, née Shen, was honored as Lady of Suitability; his birth mother was née Xin. Both parents were living. His elder brother Han was a tribute scholar. He married a woman née He. He placed first in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and 140th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Chun 林春, courtesy name Ziren, was registered in a military household of the Taizhou Battalion, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Fuqing County, Fujian. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather was Kui; his father was Hong; and his mother was née Xu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Qing. He married a woman née Li. He placed sixty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Ting, registered in a civilian household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zizheng; he ranked first in the family and was twenty-nine years old, born on the twenty-third day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Bing, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Rui; his father was Xiwen; and his mother was née Ma. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xuan, Qian, Da, and Yao; his younger brothers were Ying, Zun (a tribute scholar), Zhui (a prefectural government school student), Lin, Mai, Feng, Huan, Jin, and Yan. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Yang. He placed twenty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Mian, registered in a military household in Xiaoyi County, Fenzhou, Shanxi, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Fuzhou; he ranked first in the family and was twenty-nine years old, born on the fourth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jiulong; his grandfather was Zhu, an honorary official recognized for righteousness; his father was Dalu, a student of the Directorate of Education; his mother was née Wu; and his stepmother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Pan. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed twenty-seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Sike, registered in a civilian household in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Qixian; he ranked ninth in the family and was thirty-two years old, born on the nineteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Gong; his father was Sui, a county magistrate; his mother was née Shen; and his stepmother was née Wu. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was Sangang; his younger brothers were Wuchang, Yijing, Liude, and Sijiao. He married a woman née Li. He placed sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jia Shiyuan was registered with the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Fengxiang County, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Renfu; he ranked first in the family and was thirty years old, born on the thirteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zheng; his grandfather was Zhen; his father was Qing, an instructor in a county government school; and his mother was née Shi. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Cai. He placed twenty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

周滿〔貫四川松潘衛官籍，成都府漢州人，國子生，治詩經，字謙之，行五，年二十六，六月二十五日生〕。曾祖敏〔正千戶〕，祖文，父鸞，母張氏。具慶下，兄榮〔正千戶〕。娶黃氏。四川鄉試第四十九名，會試第四十六名。

陳乙〔貫河南開封府杞縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字子元，行一，年二十三，十一月初五日生〕。曾祖禮〔壽官〕，祖欽，父江〔貢士〕，母王氏。慈侍下，弟卜〔貢士〕、丁。娶曹氏。河南鄉試第七名，會試第二十九名。
translation_en:
Yu Zibo, registered in an artisan household in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Liqing; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-two years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Shihong (an honorary official for longevity), his grandfather Huan, his father Jin (an Imperial University student), and his mother née Shen. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Ziyi, Zikui, Zichui, Zilong, Ziyu, Zigao, and Ziji. He married a woman née Huai and was subsequently betrothed to a woman née Yao. He placed seventieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Yuzhu, registered in a military household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Bangshi; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the fourteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Li (a District Magistrate), his grandfather Gao (an honorary official for righteousness), his father Xiang, and his mother née Yu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Yulou and Yushu. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed one hundred twentieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Man, registered in an officer household of Songpan Guard, Sichuan, and a native of Hanzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Qianzhi; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was twenty-six years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Min (a Battalion Commander), his grandfather Wen, his father Luan, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother Rong was a Battalion Commander. He married a woman née Huang. He placed forty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yi, registered in a civilian household in Qi County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ziyuan; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-three years old, born on the fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Li (an honorary official for longevity), his grandfather Qin, his father Jiang (a tribute scholar), and his mother née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Bu (a tribute scholar) and Ding. He married a woman née Cao. He placed seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xie Shaonan was registered in a civilian household in Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was originally from Gan County, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yingwu; his family birth order is recorded as “二一” [?]. He was thirty-five years old, born on the fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather, Xin, was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Straightforward Service and Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of War. His grandfather, Fang, was a prefect, advanced in rank to Grand Master of Lesser Rectitude. His father was Chengju; his father's previous wives were Lady Li and Lady Jia, and his mother was Lady Tang. Both parents were deceased. He married Lady Deng. He ranked 118th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Konghua was registered in a military household in Luling County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zongzhou, and he was seventh in family birth order. He was forty years old, born on the nineteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yide; his grandfather, Qian; his father, Bao; and his mother, Lady Peng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kongyuan, Kongcheng, and Kongji. He married Lady Liu. He ranked sixty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ke Shiqing was registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An attached student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Guangzhong, and he was fourteenth in family birth order. He was twenty-eight years old, born on the fourteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shurong; his grandfather, Jing; his father, Yi; and his mother, Lady Huang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Xiuqing, and his younger brother was Qiqing. He married Lady Hong. He ranked forty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Wei was registered in an official household under the Administration Office in Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhangfu, and he was first in family birth order. He was thirty-four years old, born on the second day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zhifu; his grandfather, Fu; his father, Bi, a Ceremonial Escort; and his mother, the County Lady of Yuanling. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Wen, Shan, Ji, Jing, Shen, and Fei. He married Lady Mi. He ranked fortieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gao Shiyan, courtesy name Zhongxiu, was registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, and was an auxiliary student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents, ranked first among his brothers, and was twenty-six years old, born on the fourth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhaonan, an Imperial University student; his grandfather was Gongtang, an honorary official; his father was Gang; and his mother was Lady Tian. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shitai, Shixun, Shiqing, Shiqing 世清, and Shidu. He married Lady Zhou. He placed second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Tingxuan, courtesy name Ziyi, was registered in a military household in Xuzhou Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked sixth among his brothers, and was twenty-eight years old, born on the third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun; his grandfather was Duan, an honorary official; his father was Xiao, an Imperial University student; and his mother was Lady Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tinghui and Tingju, both Imperial University students, Tinghua, Tingli, and Tingqin; his younger brother was Tingjian. He married Lady Song. He placed sixty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Hua, courtesy name Tingbin, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked first among his brothers, and was thirty-eight years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chongshan; his grandfather was Dan, a titular official; his father was Luan; and his mother was Lady Zhou. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Ping, E, Ying, Cui, Zhang, Fan, and Cai. He married Lady Wang. He placed twenty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Weng Xueyuan, courtesy name Yuandao, was registered in a civilian household in Suichang County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked third among his brothers, and was twenty-nine years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cunren; his grandfather was Shouning; his father was Kui; his father's former wife was Lady Pan; and his mother was Lady Huang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Daoyuan and Deyuan. He married Lady Liu. He placed thirty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Jue 陳玨, courtesy name Guoxiang, was registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked forty-seventh in family order and was aged forty-three, born on the sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chubang; his grandfather, Hongzhen; his father, Yanxun; his mother, née Sha; and his birth mother, née Yang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Zhang, Rui (a director in the Ministry of Justice, with the prestige title Grand Master for Upright Service), Yu, Bo, and Po. His wife was née Weng. He placed seventy-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zuo Yi 左鎰, courtesy name Yingheng, was registered in Jing County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked seventh in family order and was aged twenty-six, born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shu; his grandfather, Dun; his father, Zan; and his mother, née Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jin, Du, Luan, Tie, Kun, and Lian; his younger brothers were Jian, Hua, Jiao, and Kuang. His wife was née Tang. He placed sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Qigao 何其高, courtesy name Yizhi, was registered in Langzhong County, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third in family order and was aged forty-three, born on the twenty-first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan; his grandfather, Guang; his father, Ming; and his mother, née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Qifeng, Tingrui, Tian’en, and Qixian; his younger brother was Tianyou. His wife was née Deng; his subsequent wives were née Yang, née Liu, and née Chen. He placed sixty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Yizhi 楊伊志, courtesy name Ziren, was registered in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. An additional-quota student at the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty-two, born on the fifth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenfu; his grandfather, Xin (posthumously appointed Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue); his father, Sheng (Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites); his mother, née Chen (granted the title Lady); and his birth mother, née He. His father was deceased and his mother living. His wife was née Chen. He placed fifty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Tang Guoxiang 唐國相, registered in an artisan household in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, was a native of Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, and an added-quota student of the Shuntian prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shunju. Second in birth order, he was aged twenty-eight and was born on the sixteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather Rong, his father Ying, and his mother née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Guodong and his younger brother Guozhu. He married a woman née Yan. He placed sixty-third in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Zonghao 周宗鎬 was registered as a government student in Baling County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, and attended the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zijing. Seventeenth in birth order, he was aged twenty-six and was born on the eighth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Youzhong, his grandfather Yibian, his father Zhi, and his mother née Fang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zonggan; his younger brothers were Zongkui, Zongqi, Zongji, Zongqing, Zongzhao, Zonglin, and Zongheng. He married a woman née Liu. He placed eighty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bai Yue 白悅, registered in an official household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard, was a native of Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhenfu. Sixth in birth order, he was aged thirty-four and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather Ke was a county-school Instructor, posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Justice. His grandfather Ang was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Justice; he retired from office and was posthumously granted the titles Specially Advanced and Grand Guardian, with the posthumous name Kangmin. His father Che was Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His mother, née He, was granted the title Lady of Virtue. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jian, an Imperial University student; Zhao, an Usher in the Court of State Ceremonial; and Tong, Jie, and Shen, all Imperial University students. His younger brothers were Dang, an Imperial University student; Yi, a student admitted by virtue of official family status; and Pu, an Imperial University student. He married a woman née Zou, subsequently a woman née Zhang, and subsequently a woman née Jiang. He placed twentieth in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shuyi 陳叔頤 was registered in a military household in Jingyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, and was a prefectural-school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zizhen. Third in birth order, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the third day of the intercalary fourth month. His great-grandfather was Chun; his grandfather Man held an honorary official title awarded for longevity; and his father Xi was a county Registrar. His father’s former wife and his mother were both née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yong and Shuzhou; his younger brothers were Shushan and Shumei, the latter a tribute scholar. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Zhao. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Zu, registered in a civilian household in Fengqiu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yizhi; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ji, his grandfather Gao, and his father Tong; his mother was née Han, and his stepmothers were née Niu and née Li. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brother was Dou, and his wife was née Fan. He ranked second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 195th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Qifan, registered in a military household in Xinghua County, Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Renqing; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li, his grandfather Gai (holder of an honorary official title for longevity), and his father Miwang; his mother was née Yu, and his stepmother née Zhu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Qi'ou, and his wife was née Huang. He ranked forty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 320th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Zhen, registered in a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an added-quota student of the prefectural school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shizhao; he was third in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the tenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather Liang was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his grandfather Yuan held those same titles. His father Tang was a student of the Directorate of Education, and his mother was née Shen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Xun (a County Magistrate) and Lie, and his wife was née Gu. He ranked 111th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Xi, registered in an officer household of Jizhou Guard and a native of Tang County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Shuntian prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Guofu; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the seventeenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Qing, grandfather An, and father Hao each held the office of Battalion Commander; his mother was née Zhao. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Wei and Yu. His wife was née Teng, and he subsequently married a woman née Dong. He ranked 111th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jiang Xin 蔣信, courtesy name Qingshi, was registered in a civilian household in Wuling County, Changde Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in family birth order, aged fifty, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Rui, his grandfather Cheng, his father Jing, and his mother née Wan; both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Jie. He married a woman née Jiang, then successively women née Li and Liu. He placed ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Pan 茅盤, courtesy name Xinzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Dantu County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered region. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in family birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the second day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather Yu held the title of Honorary Official; his father Jian held a seventh-rank prestige title. His mother was née Nie and his stepmother née Fei; his father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Jian 鑒, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Luan; his younger brothers were Fu and Jian 鋻. He married a woman née Cao and subsequently a woman née Feng. He placed 107th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Qin 范欽, courtesy name Yaoqing, was registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was fifty-fifth in family birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the nineteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Chao, his grandfather Xin was an Assistant Instructor, his father was Bi, and his mother was née Wang; both parents were living. His elder brother was Yong, and his younger brothers were Jun, Tang, Hao, Ju, Xi 鎴, and Xian. He married a woman née Yuan. He placed seventieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 178th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ming 張明, courtesy name Yuanliang, was registered in a civilian household in Pucheng County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in family birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zunmei, his grandfather Yunrang, and his father Tingzhao; his father's former wife was née Xu, and his mother was née Yang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brother was Xiu, and he married a woman née Chen. He placed forty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Shixian, registered in Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household, was a supplementary student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Bangxian; he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty-four, born on the eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Wang, his grandfather Yuanze, and his father Gang; his mother was née Lin. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shigui, Shigong, Shiyun, Shizhi, Shibao, Shihe, and Shizhen. His wife was née Dai. He placed seventy-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Huai, registered in Yongfeng County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Rude; he ranked sixty-eighth in family order and was aged forty-one, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zi'ang, his grandfather Maohui, and his father Xian; his mother was née Zhu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Heng, Kai (Prefect), Hu (a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort), and Chen; his younger brothers were Cong, Zao, Bo, Yi, Yu, Shen, Xing, and Shi. His wife was née Mao. He placed 105th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xin Tong, registered in Anqiu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household, was a student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Bingzhong; he ranked fourth in family order and was aged thirty-one, born on the fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Zeng, and his father Xiang; his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yong, Xian, and Zong. His wife was née Luan. He placed twenty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Ru was registered in a military household under the Qunmu Office in Henan and was a native of Xincheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. He was an added student of the Tangyin County Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zichun; he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty-five, born on the eighteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Gang, his grandfather Zhi, and his father Fu; his mother was née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Shi, Yi, and Ren. His wife was née Dong. He placed ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fan Se 范瑟, registered in a civilian household in Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Konghe, he was eighth in birth order, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zheng, his grandfather Sheng, and his father Fu; his father's former wife was née Kong, and his mother was née Ma. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shan, Qi, Pu〔a sacrificial official (shengjiguan)〕, Ju, Ban, Jue, and Qin; his wife was née Yang. He placed seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Liang 錢亮, registered in an artisan household in Dantu County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), was a prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Zhifu, he was fifth in birth order, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the fourth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming, his grandfather Jian, his father Yun, and his mother née Cao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Wen and Fang; his wife was née Lü. He placed fourteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yu 張愚, registered in a military household of Tianjin Left Guard in Zhili and a native of Zhucheng County, Shandong, was a guard school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Ziming, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the thirtieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shineng, his grandfather Hong, his father Feng, and his mother née Dong. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Li. He placed seventy-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Yingzhong 黃應中, registered in a civilian household in Zhongzhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zifu, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jue, his grandfather Benli, his father Bi〔a tribute student (gongshi)〕, and his mother née Lu. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Yingzheng; his wife was née Shen. He placed eleventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Sui 許檖 was registered in Lanyang County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Guohua, ranked third among his brothers, and was aged twenty-five, born on the twenty-ninth day of the second month. His great-grandfather Zhen was a county Registrar; his grandfather Kai received successive honorary appointments culminating in Director in the Ministry of Revenue. His father was Tingyou, and his mother was née Xiao; both parents were living. His elder brother Dongchun [?] was an Imperial Academy student, and his younger brothers were Ying, Jia, Zi, Mei, Nan, Gong, Ting, and Jiao. He married a woman née Niu. He placed twenty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Zhi 吳至 was registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a military household. An Imperial Academy student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he had the courtesy name Daoqing, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged twenty-nine, born on the sixth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather Qin was posthumously appointed Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice; his grandfather was Zhi 秩, his father was Zheng, and his mother was née He. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Kezhi and Xuezhi. He married a woman née Gu and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed twenty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qin Mingxia 秦鳴夏 was registered in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a military household. A prefectural school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Ziheng, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged twenty-five, born on the twenty-fifth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Zongfu; his grandfather Yanbin received an honorary appointment as Vice Director of the Office of Messengers and a posthumous appointment as Director in the Ministry of Justice. His father Li was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, and his mother was née Bao; both parents were deceased. His elder brother Mingchun was a tribute scholar, and his younger brothers were Mingqiu, Minglei, and Mingdong. He married a woman née Lin. He placed fifty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 314th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Yu 施雨 was registered in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. An Imperial Academy student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Runzhi, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-three, born on the fifteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather Qi held honorary official rank awarded for longevity; his grandfather was Rong, his father was Lun, and his mother was née Miao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jie, and his younger brothers were Yun, Dian, Lu, and Ni. He married a woman née Xue. He placed 130th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 270th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Qian 張謙 was registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An attached student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ziyi, and he ranked thirty-sixth in the family. He was thirty-two years old, born on the thirteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Shan, his grandfather Chang, his father Jin, and his mother née Liu. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Jun, an official awaiting selection for appointment, Gao, Jian, Jin, Xun, and Xu; his younger brother was Yu. His wife was née Chen. He placed eightieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Tingyin 于廷寅 was registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An attached student of the county school, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Erqing, and he ranked sixteenth in the family. He was thirty-two years old, born on the seventh day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Qingyi, a student of the Imperial University; his grandfather was Ying; and his father was Zhen, a county magistrate. His legal mother was née Shu, and his birth mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ting'e. His wife was née Yan. He placed fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yingyuan 許應元 was registered in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household, and was a native of Dong'an County, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zichun, and he ranked second in the family. He was twenty-seven years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Jiugao, his grandfather Shen, his father Guinian, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yingjue; his younger brothers were Yingkui, Yinglong, Yingxiu, Yinglu, Yingxiong, Yingqi, Yingheng, Yingde, Yingtai, Yinglin, Yingjian, Yingqiu, Yingzheng, Yingshu, and Yingyue. His wife was née Xu 徐. He placed eighty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Jilu 劉繼禄 was registered in an officer household in Yongning Guard under the Wanquan Regional Military Commission, and was a native of Sanhe County, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Chengde, and he ranked first in the family. He was thirty-eight years old, born on the sixth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather Zheng and grandfather Jun were both vice battalion commanders. His father was Xiwu, his mother née Zhang, and his stepmother née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jijue, a vice battalion commander, Jiwei, Jixiang, Jishan, and Jizhi. His first wife was née Ding; he subsequently married a woman née Lü. He placed twenty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 201st in the Metropolitan Examination.

曾大吉〔貫河南開封府陳州民籍，國子生，治春秋，字子脩，行一，年三十九，五月十九日生〕。曾祖剛，祖和〔壽官〕，父福〔義官〕，母盧氏。具慶下，弟大全、大用，娶朱氏。河南鄉試第六十八名，會試第一百六十八名。

translation_en:
Bian Shen 邊侁, registered in an official household in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xingfu; he ranked fourth in birth order and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather Yong was a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue, posthumously granted the title of left vice censor-in-chief; his grandfather Yong 鏞 was right vice minister of Justice in Nanjing; and his father Xian was prefect of Yingtian. His mother, née Zheng, was invested with the title of Lady (ruren); his stepmother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wei, salt distribution commissioner; Yi, right administration vice commissioner; Bei; Qiao, department magistrate; Xie, bureau director; Cheng, vice director of a bureau in the Ministry of Justice; and Yao, supervisor in the Court of Imperial Entertainments [?]. His younger brothers were Cai, a tribute scholar; Ren; Tan; Jia; and Pi, a tribute scholar. An extraneous “h” occurs before the list of younger brothers [?]. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huangfu Xiao 皇甫涍, registered in a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zi'an; he ranked second in birth order and was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather Xin was posthumously granted the title of vice director of a bureau in the Ministry of Rites; and his father Lu was a prefect. His mother, née Huang, was invested with the title of Lady (yiren). Both parents were living. His elder brother Chong was a tribute scholar; his younger brothers were Fang, a county magistrate, and Lian. He married a woman née Liu. He placed second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Daji 曾大吉, registered in a civilian household in Chenzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zixiu; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-nine years old, born on the nineteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Gang; his grandfather He held an honorary official title for longevity; and his father Fu held an honorary official title for charitable contributions. His mother was née Lu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Daquan and Dayong. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed sixty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 168th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Min Rulin 閔如霖, registered in a military household in Wucheng County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shiwang; he ranked fourth in birth order and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Cheng, and his father Hui; his mother was née Shen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Rusong, a student of the Imperial University, Rugui, and Rupian; his younger brothers were Runan, Ruchun, Ruwu, and Rumei. He married a woman née Huang. He placed eighty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Chun, courtesy name Yuanling, was registered in an artisan household in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in family birth order and was twenty-eight sui, born on the ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuchu; his grandfather, Yong, held the honorary designation of Official for Righteous Conduct; and his father, Lin, was a Guard Registrar. His father's principal wife was Lady Wu, his stepmother was Lady Wang, and his birth mother was Lady Ling. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xiang and his younger brother was Cai; he married Lady Zhang. He placed eighteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Hanru, courtesy name Daofu, was registered in a civilian household in Kaocheng County, Sui Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked first in family birth order and was thirty-nine sui, born on the sixteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather, Jixian, was an Imperial University student; his father, Tingzuo, was an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was Lady Ning. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Hanqing, Hanjie, Laixun, Laixuan, Laitong, Laixia, Laiju, and Laiwen; he married Lady Wang. He placed tenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 141st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yue, courtesy name Zizhi, was registered in a military officer household in Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked sixty-eighth in family birth order and was thirty-three sui, born on the third day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Siwen; his grandfather was Kongquan; his father, Guan, was an annual tribute student; and his mother was Lady Wu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Biao, Tang, Qiao, Yun, Zhang, Ying, Fei, and Xiao; his younger brother was Jue. He married Lady Zhan. He placed fortieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Xiangfeng, courtesy name Mengzhen, was registered in a military household in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked seventh in family birth order and was twenty-nine sui, born on the fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lun; his grandfather, Tang, was an Acting Instructor and a provincial graduate (juren); his father was Ji; and his mother was Lady Kong. Both parents were living. He married Lady Zhong. He placed sixty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 188th in the Metropolitan Examination.

呂瑚〔貫江西廣信府永豐縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字汝器，行三十九，年四十四，二月三十日生〕。曾祖子英，祖茂忠，父聰，母潘氏。慈侍下，兄夔〔知府〕、稷，弟璉、珂、懷〔同科進士〕，娶詹氏。江西鄉試第一百十八名，會試第一百三十四名。

趙一中〔貫直隸河間府青縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字立夫，行一，年二十九，七月初二日生〕。曾祖寬，祖榮，父璠，母蕭氏，繼母夏氏。重慶下，弟一原，娶白氏。順天府鄉試第五十六名，會試第一百二十七名。
translation_en:
Wang Heng 王珩, courtesy name Jiefu, was registered in a civilian household in Jiaohe County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in family seniority and was aged thirty-one, born on the thirteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, a Police Chief; his grandfather was Yong; his father was Hao; and his mother was née Shi. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Ju and his younger brother Li; his wife was née Zhang. He placed ninety-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Fu 毛復, courtesy name Shiheng, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked nineteenth in family seniority and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shijue; his grandfather was Huai, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; his father was Ming; his mother was née Bao; and his stepmother was née Zhou. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Xian, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and Shi 實, a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice; his younger brother was Shi 師. His wife was née Qian. He placed forty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 138th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Hu 呂瑚, courtesy name Ruqi, was registered in a civilian household in Yongfeng County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked thirty-ninth in family seniority and was aged forty-four, born on the thirtieth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziying; his grandfather was Maozhong; his father was Cong; and his mother was née Pan. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Kui, a Prefect, and Ji; his younger brothers were Lian, Ke, and Huai, the last of whom also became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in this examination year. His wife was née Zhan. He placed 118th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 134th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Yizhong 趙一中, courtesy name Lifu, was registered in a civilian household in Qing County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in family seniority and was aged twenty-nine, born on the second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kuan; his grandfather was Rong; his father was Fan; his mother was née Xiao; and his stepmother was née Xia. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Yiyuan, and his wife was née Bai. He placed fifty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yong Lan, registered in an artisan household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Sidao; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged forty-one, born on the twenty-second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zhizheng; his grandfather, Guiyu, received the honorary title of Guard Registrar; his father, Ruhe, was a Superintendent; and his mother, née Chen, received the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Hong and Jing, and his younger brothers Kun and Li. His wife was née Chen. He placed forty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ouyang Qing, registered in a civilian household in Shangrao County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Maozhi; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-one, born on the fourteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Wenxin; his grandfather, Jiuzhen; his father, Gui, an Assistant Instructor; his mother, née Hu; and his stepmother, née Jia. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Hong, and his wife was née Lian. He placed thirty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 170th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Cheng, registered in an officer household of the Nanjing Central Palace Guard and a native of Taoyuan County, Huguang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Quanqing; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the thirtieth day of the third month. His great-grandfather Fu, grandfather Hai, and father Kuan were all Company Commanders; his mother was née Li. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Wu, a Company Commander, Wei, Shi, and Zhi. His wife was née Xu. He placed forty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yue, registered in a civilian household in Wenshang County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Ruqiao; he ranked ninth among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Congshan; his grandfather, Gui; his father, Xian; and his mother, née Jiang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chong, Song, Yan (巖), Ling, Kun, Xiu, Lan, and Yan (嵒). His wife was née Wang. He placed ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 107th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wei Yuanque, registered in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shaoqian; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the sixteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather, Shizuo, held an honorary title for longevity; and his father was Ying. His father's former wife was née Huang, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yuanshuo, Yuanxiang, Yuanzhu, Yuandong, Yuangui, and Yuanyi. His wife was née Luo. He placed forty-seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 183rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pu Yingqi, registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Daozheng; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-third day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Sen; his grandfather, Zongsheng, held an honorary title for public beneficence; and his father, Jin, was a county magistrate. His mother was née Huang. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Yingyuan, Yingchen, and Yingdeng. His wife was née Lu. He placed fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Yi, registered in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a salt-producing household and was an added student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziheng; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged twenty-one, born on the fifteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather, Duan, held an honorary title for longevity; his grandfather, Bi, was posthumously granted the title of Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Military Affairs; and his father, Han, was Right Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission. His mother, née Lu, was granted the title of Lady of Courtesy. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chuan, Xie, and Cheng. His wife was née Zhang. He placed forty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Duan Cheng'en, registered in Jinning Subprefecture, Yunnan Prefecture, Yunnan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Defu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the nineteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jixiang; his grandfather was Jun; and his father, Yongsheng, held an honorary title for public beneficence. His mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chengchong and Chengjue. His wife was née Zhao; he subsequently married a woman née Li. He placed second in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

曾祖惇思　祖祚〔義官〕　父璟　前母諸氏　母陳氏

陳禎〔貫江西撫州府崇仁縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字大和，行一，年四十，十二月十三日生〕。曾祖復暘，祖汝篪，父公翰，母李氏。具慶下，弟祥，娶李氏。江西鄉試第二十三名，會試第一百五十四名。

邵元吉〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字德旋，行六，年三十二，六月二十八日生〕。曾祖悌思，祖祚〔義官〕，父穧，前母諸氏，母陳氏。永感下，兄元臣、元善、元亨、元廉，弟元仁、元祥，娶沈氏。浙江鄉試第十四名，會試第二百九十三名。
translation_en:
You Jujing, registered in Nanping County, Yanping Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xingjian; he ranked twenty-second among his brothers and male cousins and was twenty-four years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tingci, his grandfather You, and his father Lun, a student of the National University; his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zhujing, and his wife was née Li. He placed sixty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 213th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Xu, registered in Gaoyang County, Anzhou Subprefecture, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Demao; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty-one years old, born on the first day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dechun, his grandfather Jing, a county Registrar, and his father He; his mother was née Guo. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Dan, Zui, and Bian, and his wife was née Li. He placed second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 102nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zhen, registered in Chongren County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Dahe; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was forty years old, born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuyang, his grandfather Ruchi, and his father Gonghan; his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Xiang, and his wife was née Li. He placed twenty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 154th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shao Yuanji, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Dexuan; he ranked sixth among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tisi, his grandfather Zuo, an honorary official, and his father Ji; his father's former wife was née Zhu, and his mother was née Chen. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yuanchen, Yuanshan, Yuanheng, and Yuanlian; his younger brothers were Yuanren and Yuanxiang. His wife was née Shen. He placed fourteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wen Heng 文衡 was registered in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, in the civilian registration category. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Gongru, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-six years old and was born on the fifth day of the sixth month.

His great-grandfather was Wen Li〔holder of an honorary office for longevity〕; his grandfather was Wen Tingfu〔County Vice Magistrate〕; his father was Wen Zixian; and his mother was née Yang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His younger brothers were Qu, Wei, Bing, Yan, Zao, Lan, and Yi. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Mu 母 [?].

He placed forty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

李延康〔貫山西潞安府民籍，國子生，治禮記，字允吉，行四，年三十三，九月十二日生〕。曾祖志美，祖翥〔知縣〕，父玹〔縣丞〕，前母王氏，母馮氏。具慶下，兄延纓、延昌、延馨〔推官〕，娶牛氏。山西鄉試第五十七名，會試第二百八十名。

潘高〔貫山西寧化守禦千戶所官籍，直隸合肥縣人，太原府學增廣生，治書經，字子抑，行一，年十九，十二月初一日生〕。曾祖政〔正千戶，封武德將軍〕，祖璟〔正千戶，封武德將軍〕，父承爵〔正千戶〕，母江氏。重慶下，弟瞻、柱、鰲、登、鵬，聘王氏。山西鄉試第四十三名，會試第二百二十七名。
translation_en:
Third class: 233 men, granted the status of graduates equivalent to metropolitan graduates (jinshi).

Yu Guang, courtesy name Huizhi, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was a native of Qimen County. A student of the Yingtian prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongliang; his grandfather, Shiying; and his father, Long. His father's principal wife was née Wang, and his birth mother was née Wu. His father was deceased and his mother living. He married a woman née Xie and subsequently a woman née Huang. He placed fiftieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yankang, courtesy name Yunji, was registered in a civilian household in Lu'an Prefecture, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twelfth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhimei; his grandfather, Zhu, was a county magistrate; and his father, Xuan, was a county vice magistrate. His father's former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Feng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yanying, Yanchang, and Yanxin, a prefectural judge. He married a woman née Niu. He placed fifty-seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Gao, courtesy name Ziyi, was registered in an officer household of the Ninghua Guard Battalion in Shanxi and was a native of Hefei County in Zhili. An additional student of the Taiyuan prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged nineteen, and born on the first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Zheng, and grandfather, Jing, were both battalion commanders granted the honorary title General of Military Virtue. His father, Chengjue, was a battalion commander, and his mother was née Jiang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Zhan, Zhu, Ao, Deng, and Peng. He was betrothed to a woman née Wang. He placed forty-third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Xian, courtesy name Rujing, was registered in a civilian household in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was second in family order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the sixteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather Zhongyi was a County Magistrate; his grandfather Sui was a County Magistrate, successively granted posthumous titles culminating in Right Assistant Censor-in-chief of the Censorate; his father Tianhe was Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His mother, née Wang, held the title Lady of Respect. Both parents were living. His elder brother Song was a tribute scholar; his younger brothers were Piao, Mu, Shu, and Luan. He married a woman née Wan; no subsequent betrothal had yet been arranged. He placed fortieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Kai, courtesy name Shanfu, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A National University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was eighteenth in family order, aged thirty-one, and born on the seventeenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Lin; his grandfather Pian held the honorary designation Official for Righteousness; his father was Xuan, and his mother was née Wenren. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Jian, Tan (Deputy Superintendent of a Salt Tax Office), Zeng, Jie, Wenkui (Supervisor in the Court of Imperial Entertainments), Da, and Cheng; his younger brothers were Feng, Chi, Pei, and Hao. He married a woman née Pan. He placed fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Tinggan, courtesy name Weizhen, was registered in a civilian household in Jing County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was third in family order, aged seventeen, and born on the fourteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Da was a Prefect; his grandfather was Pu; his father was Ruyou, and his mother was née Zhao. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Shu and Long; his younger brothers were Tingjie, Ying, Zi, Wu, Zhang, Ji, Li, Fei, Hang, and Lan. He was betrothed to a woman née Zuo. He placed fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 158th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Tianqi, courtesy name Yizhan, was registered in a civilian household in Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. A National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was seventy-fifth in family order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twelfth day of the intercalary fourth month. His great-grandfather was Guigao; his grandfather Yuan was an Assistant Administration Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; his father Zhang was a County Magistrate, and his mother was née Xia. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tianjing, Tianxiang, Tianyou, Tianlin, Tianxi, Tianshen, and Tianjue; his younger brothers were Tianxiang and Tianfan. He married a woman née Xu. He placed twenty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.
