魏尚純〔貫河南儀衛司官籍，山東滕縣人，鈞州學生，治禮記，字叔誠，行三，年二十四，十月十五日生〕。曾祖通，祖興，父宗〔典仗〕，母張氏。具慶下，兄尚經、尚綸〔貢士〕，弟尚絅，娶白氏，繼聘李氏。河南鄉試第十九名，會試第二百二十三名。

李徵〔貫湖廣常德府桃源縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字誠之，行三，年二十六，九月十九日生〕。曾祖茂堅，祖暹，父冕〔京縣主簿〕，母謝氏，生母周氏。慈侍下，兄岳、隆、嵩、崑、峯、崙、凾，弟徽〔訓術〕，娶宋氏。湖廣鄉試第四十八名，會試第一百十五名。
translation_en:
Zheng Jifu, registered in a military household in Luoshan County, Xinyang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Xixian, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-nine, born on the fifth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wenbin (a police-office official [?], the title being abbreviated); his grandfather was Ji; his father was Hong (an honorary official); his father's former wives were née Zhao and née Qu, and his mother was née Shang. His mother was living and his father deceased; his elder brother was Zhong, and his younger brothers were Guangfu and Xingfu. He married a woman née Wang and placed thirtieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jing, registered in a military household of the Front Imperial Guard and a native of Gaoyou Subprefecture in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the capital guards' military school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Deshi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Ji (a Registrar); his grandfather was Ye; his father was Min (a titular official); his mother was née Ji, and his stepmother was née Luo. His parents and grandparents were living; his younger brothers were Yunpeng and Yunrui. He married a woman née Sun and subsequently a woman née Tang, and placed fortieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 135th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Shangchun, registered in an official household of the Henan Ceremonial Guard Office and a native of Teng County, Shandong, was a government student of Junzhou specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Shucheng, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-four, born on the fifteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather was Xing; his father was Zong (a Ceremonial Guard); and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living; his elder brothers were Shangjing and Shanglun (a tribute scholar), and his younger brother was Shangjiong. He married a woman née Bai and was subsequently betrothed to a woman née Li, and placed nineteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zheng, registered in a civilian household in Taoyuan County, Changde Prefecture, Huguang, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Chengzhi, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-six, born on the nineteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Maojian; his grandfather was Xian; his father was Mian (Registrar of a capital county); his mother was née Xie, and his birth mother was née Zhou. His mother was living and his father deceased; his elder brothers were Yue, Long, Song, Kun, Feng, Lun, and Han, and his younger brother was Hui (an Instructor in the county Daoist registry). He married a woman née Song and placed forty-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

沈伯咸〔貫浙江嘉興府秀水縣民籍，嘉善縣人，國子生，治書經，字公甫，行二，年三十七，四月十五日生〕。曾祖真卿，祖逹〔壽官〕，父潮，母繆氏。具慶下，兄伯良，娶張氏，繼娶徐氏、張氏。浙江鄉試第四十名，會試第一百四十四名。

translation_en:
Li Chengyun 李乗雲, registered in a civilian household in Junzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the department school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Ziyu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-six, born on the eleventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Gang, his grandfather Quan, his father Yan, and his mother née Zhou; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Dengyun, Lingyun, Piyun, Wangyun, Qingyun, and Canyun, and his wife was née Liu. He placed forty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

You Lu 尤魯, registered in a civilian household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Maozong, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-third day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather Huan, his father Ji, his mother née Zhou, and his stepmother née Lu; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Ne and Zhi, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed sixty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 203rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Boxian 沈伯咸, registered in a civilian household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and a native of Jiashan County, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Gongfu, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the fifteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zhenqing, his grandfather Da〔an honorary official recognized for longevity〕, his father Chao, and his mother née Miao; both parents were living, his elder brother was Boliang, and he married a woman née Zhang, subsequently marrying women née Xu and née Zhang. He placed fortieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 144th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Jun 曾鈞, registered in a civilian household in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tinghe, he ranked eighth among his brothers, and he was aged forty-three, born on the twenty-fifth day of the intercalary ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yiru, his grandfather Youmian, his father Wenxian, and his mother née Fu; both parents were deceased, his elder brothers were Tingkui, Ting’ao, Tingfan, Tingshi, and Tinggao, and his wife was née Fu. He placed fifty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Hao, registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an supplementary student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zhongjing, he ranked first in family order, and he was aged twenty-three, born on the twenty-fifth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, Instructor in the School of Yin and Yang; his grandfather was Xu, a prestige official; his father was Wenjin, a tribute scholar; and his mother was née Zhang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Ke, and his younger brothers were Jian, Zhao, Han, and Xuan. His wife was née Zhao. He placed sixty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Zizheng, registered in a military household in Liu’an Subprefecture, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Ruzhong, he ranked first in family order, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yue, an Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Tong, an honorary official recognized for righteousness; his father was Rui, a Messenger in the Messenger Office; and his mother was née Wu. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His younger brothers were Ziru, Zixiao, and Zi’an. His wife was née Zhang. He placed ninety-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Rubi, registered in a civilian household in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Weiliang, he ranked sixth in family order, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zongyan, his grandfather was Cheng, his father was Jun, a District Magistrate, and his mother was née Hu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ruyi, Ruming, and Rucong, and his younger brother was Ruxian. His wife was née Tu. He placed thirty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Mai, registered in a military household in Rong County, Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Dezhong, he ranked first in family order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Bocheng; his grandfather was Ding, a District Vice Magistrate; his father was Shang, an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Liu; and his stepmother was née Zhang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Jian, and his younger brothers were Yan, Ping, Xiang, Lang, Ying, and Jin. His wife was née Yang. He placed twenty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Yixiang, registered in Fengyang County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zhongyu. Second in birth order, he was thirty-eight years old and was born on the fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather, Ji, held an honorary longevity title; and his father, Long, was an Assistant Instructor. His mother was née Xu, and his stepmother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Yi'ao, was a Chief Medical Officer; his younger brothers were Yiju and Yiming. He married a woman née Gao and subsequently a woman née Dai. He placed eightieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Jing, registered in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the county school. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Shuming. First in birth order, he was twenty-eight years old and was born on the twenty-second day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Aitong; his grandfather, Lei, was an Instructor; his father was Shizheng, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Lun, Wei, and Cai. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Wei was registered in an official household of Hejian Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region and was a native of Fengrun County, Shuntian Prefecture. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Deyu. Second in birth order, he was forty-five years old and was born on the nineteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather was Cong; his father was Qin, and his mother was née Guo. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Sheng, and his younger brother was Ling. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Yang. He placed sixteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mi Rong, registered in Shaowu County, Shaowu Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Renfu. First in birth order, he was forty-seven years old and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youwen; his grandfather was Weibao; his father was Liuzhu, and his mother was née Tang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Hua. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and two hundred sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hu Jing, registered in a civilian household in Ruyang County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education who specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yubo; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fourth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yicheng, posthumously appointed an Examining Editor in the Hanlin Academy; his grandfather was Shan, an Adviser promoted to Administrator, with the prestige title Grand Master for Deliberation, rank 5a; and his father was Yongfang, a District Magistrate. His legal mother was née Li, and his birth mother was née Jing. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Kun, and he married a woman née Li. He placed forty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Runan, registered in a military household in Tong'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education who specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Mengcai; he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fifth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Daliang; his grandfather was Tingli, an Official for Righteousness, an honorary designation; his father was Zuo; and his mother was née Wang. His parents and grandparents were living. He married a woman née Huang. He placed first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Ying, registered in a civilian household in Wushan County, Kuizhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education who specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zizhong; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the seventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Wen; his grandfather was Lin, a student of the Directorate of Education; his father was Maozhu; and his mother was née Huang. His father was deceased and his mother living. He married a woman née Xiang. He placed thirty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ce, registered in a civilian household in Zhongzhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education who specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yide; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the eighteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Jian, posthumously appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; his grandfather was Rui, Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; his father was Dashao; and his mother was née Ma. Both parents were living. His elder brother was En, and his younger brothers were Zhen and Huang. He married a woman née Gu. He placed fifty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 152nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳脩〔貫浙江紹興府山陰縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字宗道，行二，年三十八，十一月初十日生〕。曾祖賢，祖珪，父清，母趙氏，繼母鄭氏。具慶下，兄朋，娶王氏。浙江鄉試第三十八名，會試第三十五名。
translation_en:
Wang Jizong, registered in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruxiao; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged forty-three, and was born on the seventeenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Gan; his grandfather, Ru, was an Imperial University student; his father was Fen, and his mother was Lady Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shaozong, a Steward of Food, Wanhua, and Ruyi, an Imperial University student. His younger brothers were Zuanzong, Shengzong, Xuzong, Tongzong, Zengzong, and Bian, a tribute scholar. The following words, “適繼承唐氏,” are unclear, though they mention Lady Tang [?]; he had not yet arranged a subsequent marriage [?]. He placed twenty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Ruzhou, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yiji; he ranked seventh among his brothers, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the fourth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Kemin; his grandfather was Zhizhong; his father was Yancun, and his mother was Lady Huang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Rujin, Ruda, Ruheng, Rucheng, Ruyi, and Ruxuan. He married Lady Huang. He placed eighty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhai Hao, registered in a military banner household of Zhennan Guard and originally from Dongguan County, Guangdong, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhoufu; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Danzhi; his grandfather, Rong, and father, Quan, were both platoon commanders accorded the cap and girdle of official status. His mother was Lady Shi. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhen and Jian, and his younger brothers were Yue and Qin. He married Lady Wang. He placed 227th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xiu, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zongdao; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the tenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather was Gui; his father was Qing; his mother was Lady Zhao, and his stepmother was Lady Zheng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Peng. He married Lady Wang. He placed thirty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

周琉〔貫湖廣德安府應城縣民籍，京山縣人，國子生，治詩經，字潤夫，行四，年三十六，十二月十八日生〕。曾祖韶，祖域，父倣〔府同知，進階奉政大夫〕，母陳氏。具慶下，弟玧、珖，娶郭氏。湖廣鄉試第十二名，會試第一百九十八名。
translation_en:
He Si, registered in a civilian household in Xiong County, Baoding Prefecture, the Metropolitan Region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shenzhi; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-five sui, born on the fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Wang, and his father Lu, a county magistrate; his mother was née Han. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Lü, Gan, Ying, Nian, Ci, Zhi, and Ren, and his wife was née Su. He placed sixty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 288th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Lian, registered in a civilian household in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, the Metropolitan Region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yingkui; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-two sui, born on the fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Zan, and his father Liang; his mother was née Zhang and his stepmother née Gao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhi, and his younger brothers were Ling, Pin, and Geng; his wife was née Zhang. He placed sixty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lai Ruxian, registered in a salt-producing household in Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ziyu; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-one sui, born on the eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Fang, and his father Dong; his mother was née Sun. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Ruzhou, Ruming, Ruli, Ruting, Ruli (汝立), and Ruzhi, and his wife was née Qian. He placed second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Liu, registered in a civilian household in Yingcheng County, De'an Prefecture, Huguang, and a native of Jingshan County, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Runfu; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty-six sui, born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shao, his grandfather Yu, and his father Fang, a prefectural vice prefect promoted to the rank of Grand Master for Governance; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yun and Guang, and his wife was née Guo. He placed twelfth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Shiheng 張世亨, courtesy name Daqing, was registered in a civilian household in Anping County, Jinzhou Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; he was a county government student specializing in the Classic of Changes, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged twenty-three, born on the twelfth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guo, his grandfather Jian, and his father Qi; his mother was née Li and his stepmother née Fan; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Shilong and Shiguang, his wife was née Lü, and he placed 123rd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Jin 徐進, courtesy name Yuke, was registered in a military household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Min, his grandfather Long, his father Hua, and his mother née Huang; his grandparents and parents were living, his younger brothers were Qian and Di, his wife was née Chen, and he placed fifty-third in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Shiyong 劉世用, courtesy name Ruxian, was registered in a civilian household in Shulu County, Qizhou Subprefecture, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty, born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Quan, his grandfather Liang, his father Xian, and his mother née Zhao; both parents were living, his elder brother was Shiqian and his younger brothers Shihao, Shizheng, and Shixuan, his wife was née Wang, and he placed fifty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dang Chengci 党承賜, courtesy name Ruxi, was registered in a military household in Xinzhou Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, ranked fourth among his brothers, and was aged thirty-four, born on the seventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, a subprefectural vice magistrate; his grandfather was Yongling, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his father was Mao, a county magistrate who received successive honorary grants culminating in Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel; and his mother was née Man [?], who received successive grants of the title Lady of Suitability (yiren); his father alone was living, his elder brothers were Chengzhi, Right Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission, Chengmei, a county magistrate, Cheng'en, a Seal Keeper, and Chenglu, his younger brothers were Chengxue, a Food Service Officer, Chengxuan, an Imperial University student, and Chengzhou, his wife was née Wang, and he placed twenty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Jiao, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a native of Shanghai County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Daoxiu and was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, born on the eighteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather Zong, and his father Shan, a Medical Instructor; his mother was née Jiang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Zheng, and his wife was née Jiang. He placed fifty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chang Yingwen, registered in Yushe County, Liao Subprefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Rushi and was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, born on the thirtieth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Xian, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; his grandfather was Jing, a District Magistrate who was honorifically invested as an Investigating Censor; and his father was Zai, a Prefect. His father's former wife, née Li, his mother, also née Li, and his stepmother, née Tian, were each invested with the title of Lady (Ruren). His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Yingkui; his younger brothers were Yingyuan, a Steward of Provisions; Yingqi, a titular official; Yingzhou, an honorary official recognized for public benefactions; Yingen, a titular official; Yingrong; Yingzhi; Yinghe; Yingchun; and Yinglin. His wife was née Zhou. He placed fifteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Cunren, registered in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household. A prefectural government school student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he had the courtesy name Bogang and was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, born on the fifteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Mo, his grandfather Hao, his father Qiming, and his mother née Qian. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Cunli, Yunjing, Jia, Yi, and Cunxing; his wife was née Sheng. He placed nineteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 153rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Gongmao, registered in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Yiqian and was second in birth order, aged twenty-four, born on the twelfth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Can, his grandfather Xiang, his father Tingchen, and his mother née Chen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Songmao and Demao; his wife was née Xu. He placed sixty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jia Shu, registered in Shanghe County, Wuding Subprefecture, Ji’nan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Shenqing. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-five and was born on the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin, Director of Works in a princely establishment; his grandfather was Ting, a Prefectural School Professor; his father was Deng, and his mother was née Xu. He had living grandparents and parents. His younger brothers were Xiang and Zhen, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed sixty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Tingchai, registered in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zipei. Second in birth order, he was aged twenty-six and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhengli, holder of a seventh-rank prestige title; his grandfather was Yin; his father was Chong, a tribute scholar (gongshi), posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; and his mother was née Zhang, granted the title Lady of Peace. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Tingzhi, Secretary in the Ministry of Justice, and his wife was née Wu. He placed thirty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 190th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Peng, registered in Chaoyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Tuanzhi. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-four and was born on the fourteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather was Quan; his father was Wenshi, and his mother was née Lin. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Feng, his younger brother was He, and his wife was née Xie. He placed fifty-sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Fei, registered in Handan County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Tizhou. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the nineteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin, an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather was Xi, Vice Minister of a Branch Court of the Imperial Stud; his father was Han, and his mother was née Tan. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Gai, an Imperial University student; his younger brother was Qu, and his wife was née Xie. He placed eleventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Su, courtesy name Wenzhi, was registered as a civilian in Shenze County, Qizhou, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Record of Rites, he was first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather Da, his father Jie, and his mother née Li. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Jiao. He ranked 110th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 61st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Qing, courtesy name Keguo, was registered as a civilian in Yanjin County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Liang, his father Pu, and his mother née Wei. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Mi (a tribute scholar), Xiangbin (an Imperial University student), Ding, Guan, Shou (an Imperial University student), Huan, and Wan [division of names uncertain]. He married a woman née He. He ranked 25th in the Henan Provincial Examination and 44th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Kui, courtesy name Meifu, was registered in the guardsman category with the Sichuan Ceremonial Guard Office and was a native of Linshui County, Shunqing Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shi, his grandfather Wen, his father Wen, and his mother née Xin. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhi and Hui. He married a woman née Du and subsequently a woman née Xu. He ranked 58th in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Wei, courtesy name Rujing, was registered as a civilian in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kongxun (honorarily appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice), his grandfather Maoyuan (a Director in the Ministry of Justice), his father Dawu, and his mother née Zhu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shi and Ru. He married a woman née Lin. He ranked 48th in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

殷學〔貫山東兖州府東平州東阿縣匠籍，國子生，治詩經，字成甫，行二，年三十，正月十一日生〕。曾祖貴，祖清，父祐，母周氏。慈侍下，兄儒，弟舉，娶張氏。山東鄉試第三十六名，會試第三十二名。

傅頤〔貫湖廣沔陽衛官籍，河南息縣人，州學增廣生，治書經，字觀蒙，行五，年二十三，二月二十四日生〕。曾祖珉〔指揮僉事〕，祖俊，父昇，母陳氏。具慶下，兄鶚、預、顯〔指揮僉事〕、頊，娶王氏，繼娶楊氏。湖廣鄉試第一名，會試第三百十名。

translation_en:
Chen Shu 陳澍, courtesy name Boyu, was registered in a military household in Hefei County, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili); he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged forty-two, born on the eleventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chi, his grandfather Qi, his father Chun, and his mother née Wang; both parents were living; his elder brother was Lan and his younger brothers Ying and Qian; he married a woman née Zhang and placed 119th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 89th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Xue 殷學, courtesy name Chengfu, was registered in an artisan household in Dong’e County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty, born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Qing, his father You, and his mother née Zhou; his mother alone was living; his elder brother was Ru and his younger brother Ju; he married a woman née Zhang and placed 36th in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 32nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Yi 傅頤, courtesy name Guanmeng, was registered in an officer household of the Mianyang Guard, Huguang, and came from Xi County, Henan; he was an added-quota student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, ranked fifth among his brothers, and was aged twenty-three, born on the twenty-fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Min, an Assistant Commander; his grandfather was Jun, his father Sheng, and his mother née Chen; both parents were living; his elder brothers were E, Yu, Xian (an Assistant Commander), and Xu; he married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Yang, and placed first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 310th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Shijie 俞世潔, courtesy name Yuzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian; he was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-nine, born on the tenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jishan, his grandfather Jing (a Post Station Master), his father Tizhong (an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions), and his mother née Xu; his mother alone was living; his elder brother was Shiyuan and his younger brothers Shilian, Shihan, and Shihao; he married a woman née Zhao and placed 40th in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

李朝陽〔貫山西太原府清源縣軍籍，國子生，治書經，字伯鳴，行一，年三十八，二月二十七日生〕。曾祖賢〔壽官〕，祖子實，父梅〔巡檢〕，母梁氏。重慶下，弟遇陽、荷陽，娶米氏，繼娶王氏。山西鄉試第九名，會試第六十名。

韓岳〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣民籍，縣學生，治禮記，字鎮伯，行一，年三十四，五月初十日生〕。曾祖循，祖永，父棣，母魯氏。永感下，弟元、稷、愷、益、皐、官、賢、夔、旦、牧、伊，娶毛氏。浙江鄉試第八十一名，會試第一百九十二名。

趙愈和〔貫江西南康府星子縣民籍，府學生，治詩經，字以禮，行三，年三十二，三月十二日生〕。曾祖駿〔衛經歷〕，祖纓，父廷宣〔訓導〕，母錢氏，繼母王氏。具慶下，兄愈良、愈充，弟愈儒、愈生，娶李氏。江西鄉試第四十一名，會試第二百九十八名。
translation_en:
Li Chaoyang, courtesy name Boming, was registered in a military household in Qingyuan County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xian, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Zishi; his father was Mei, a Police Chief; and his mother was née Liang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Yuyang and Heyang. He married a woman née Mi and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Yue, courtesy name Zhenbo, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the tenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Xun; his grandfather was Yong; his father was Di; and his mother was née Lu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Yuan, Ji, Kai, Yi, Gao, Guan, Xian, Kui, Dan, Mu, and Yi. He married a woman née Mao. He placed eighty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Rui, courtesy name Xundian, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zan; his grandfather was Gu; his father was Zhuan; his mother was née Weng; and his stepmother was née Wu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Xuan, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; Yu; Zuo; Jing; Ran; Qing; and Ning, a tribute scholar. His younger brothers were Xian, Gong, and Bi. He married a woman née Qiu. He placed eighty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Yuhe, courtesy name Yili, was registered in a civilian household in Xingzi County, Nankang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the twelfth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Jun, a Guard Command Registrar; his grandfather was Ying; his father was Tingxuan, an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Qian; and his stepmother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yuliang and Yuchong, and his younger brothers were Yuru and Yusheng. He married a woman née Li. He placed forty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

唐曜〔貫四川敘州府富順縣民籍，江西南昌縣人，國子生，治詩經，字幼貞，行十五，年二十三，九月十七日生〕。曾祖邦顯，祖淵，父公正，嫡母胡氏，生母吳氏。慈侍下，娶萬氏。四川鄉試第七名，會試第三百十三名。
translation_en:
Liao Xiyan, registered in a military household in Chaling Subprefecture, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the subprefectural school and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shuyu; he ranked second in his family and was twenty-four, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Wu'ang, his grandfather Benxiang, and his father Ye; his mother was née Bao and his stepmother née Kong. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Xizeng, Xizhou, Ximeng, and Xikui. He married a woman née Yang. He placed thirty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 305th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Kai, registered in a civilian household in Hui'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Kexie; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-six, born on the fourth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Qin, his grandfather Pu, and his father Jing; his mother was née Zeng. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Ti, Shen, and Huan. He married a woman née Wu. He placed second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Ximeng was registered in a medical household attached to the Imperial Medical Service and was a native of Wujin County in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was an added student of the Shuntian prefectural school and specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zichun; he ranked third in his family and was twenty-five, born on the eleventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Qi, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather Ning was granted the title of Assistant Commissioner of the Imperial Medical Service; and his father Jie was formerly Commissioner of the Imperial Medical Service. His father's earlier wives were née Zhou and née Li, the latter granted the title Lady of Peace. His mother was née Zhu, also granted the title Lady of Peace, and his stepmother was née Liao. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Xiyan and Xizeng, both physicians entitled to wear official caps and girdles; his younger brothers were Xizhou and Xicheng. He married a woman née Wang. He placed 115th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 205th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Yao, registered in a civilian household in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was a native of Nanchang County, Jiangxi. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Youzhen; he ranked fifteenth in his family and was twenty-three, born on the seventeenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Bangxian, his grandfather Yuan, and his father Gongzheng; his father's principal wife was née Hu and his birth mother née Wu. His mother alone was living. He married a woman née Wan. He placed seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 313th in the Metropolitan Examination.

王鉞〔貫福建福州中衛官籍，候官縣學生，治春秋，字公儀，行七，年三十四，十一月二十二日生〕。曾祖智〔贈都察院右副都御史〕，祖贊，父昇〔教諭〕，母黃氏。永感下，兄鎰、鐸〔驛丞〕、欽〔戶部主事〕，弟鍵〔貢士〕，娶陳氏。福建鄉試第六十二名，會試第一百八十四名。

胡鰲〔貫湖廣辰州府沅陵縣軍籍，府學生，治易經，字巨卿，行三，年二十八，七月初五日生〕。曾祖琥〔醫學正科〕，祖謐〔醫學正科〕，父應相〔醫學正科〕，母李氏。永感下，兄鏜、鈞，弟汝鑰、汝鍵、鯊，娶何氏。湖廣鄉試第三名，會試第三百八名。
translation_en:
Su Zhigao, registered in an artisan household in Gu’an County, Shuntian Prefecture, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Deming, and he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins. He was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Lun, and his father Ziliang; his mother was née Song. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His wife was née Wen. He placed third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yue, registered in an officer household of the Fuzhou Central Guard in Fujian, was a Houguan County school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Gongyi, and he ranked seventh among his brothers and male cousins. He was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhi was posthumously appointed Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate; his grandfather was Zan, and his father Sheng was a county school Instructor. His mother was née Huang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yi, Duo, a Station Master, and Qin, a Bureau Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his younger brother Jian was a Metropolitan Examination graduate (gongshi). His wife was née Chen. He placed sixty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Xiumin, registered in a civilian household in Xi’an County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tianyu, and he ranked twenty-seventh among his brothers and male cousins. He was twenty-eight years old, born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Weiqian, his grandfather Duan was a Department Magistrate, and his father was Biao; his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shunmin and Jimin. His wife was née Cai. He placed fifty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Ao, registered in a military household in Yuanling County, Chenzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Juqing, and he ranked third among his brothers and male cousins. He was twenty-eight years old, born on the fifth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Hu, grandfather Mi, and father Yingxiang each served as a Director of Medicine. His mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tang and Jun; his younger brothers were Ruyue, Rujian, and Sha. His wife was née He. He placed third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and three hundred eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

李文鳳〔貫廣西慶遠衛官籍，湖廣桃源縣人，國子生，治禮記，字廷儀，行四，年三十三，十一月初十日生〕。曾祖輝〔指揮僉事〕，祖顯〔知縣〕，父崙〔學正〕，母彭氏，繼母史氏。具慶下，兄文獻〔知縣〕、霖〔指揮同知〕、霽〔前貢士〕、文萌、文英，弟文德、文瓚〔貢士〕、文黼、文繡，娶王氏，繼娶韋氏。廣西鄉試第一名，會試第二百七名。

translation_en:
Ma Ruzhang, registered in a civilian household in Ji County, Weihui Prefecture, Henan, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Cunmei, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was twenty-eight years old, born on the ninth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zheng, posthumously appointed Assistant Prefect; his grandfather was Ying, a Subprefect; his father was Tu, a tribute student (gongshi); and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Ruyang, a Ceremonial Companion (consort of an imperial clanswoman), and Ruyi. His wife was née Li. He placed thirty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 164th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Xi, registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a supplementary student in the county government school specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Shiji, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Gong, a Left Assistant Administration Commissioner; his grandfather was Tai, an honorary official for public benefactions; his father was Rong, a County Registrar; and his mother was née Dong. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shiyang, and his wife was née Ye. He placed fiftieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Wenfeng, registered in an official household of Qingyuan Guard, Guangxi, and originally from Taoyuan County, Huguang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Tingyi, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was thirty-three years old, born on the tenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Hui, an Assistant Commander; his grandfather was Xian, a District Magistrate; his father was Lun, a School Instructor; his mother was née Peng, and his stepmother was née Shi. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wenxian, a District Magistrate; Lin, a Vice Commander; Ji, a former tribute student; Wenmeng; and Wenying. His younger brothers were Wende; Wenzan, a tribute student; Wenfu; and Wenxiu. His first wife was née Wang, and his subsequent wife was née Wei. He placed first in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Kui, registered in a civilian household in Pujiang County, Qiong Subprefecture, Sichuan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yingchen, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was thirty-six years old, born on the eleventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zhixian, his grandfather was Ding, his father was Boxuan, his mother was née Liu, and his stepmother was née Shao. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His wife was née Lu. He placed fifty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
He Jigao, registered in a civilian household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a supplementary student at the Qiantang County school. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Sishou; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-four years old, born on the seventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather Cong held the titles Grand Master for Upright Counsel and Administrator for Assisting Governance and served as Left Vice Minister of War; his grandfather Gang was an Examiner in the Censorate. His father was Jingfu, and his mother was née Zhu. His mother alone survived. His younger brothers were Jizeng and Jizu. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fifty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 312th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Rulun, registered in a military household of the Taicang Guard in the directly administered region, was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Dexuan; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-first day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather Ding held an honorary official title granted for longevity; his grandfather was Zhang, and his father was Qi. His mother was née Wang, and his stepmother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yi and Jing. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Ding. He placed fifty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 232nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Geng, registered in a military household of the Yuzhou Guard under the Wanquan Regional Military Commission, was a native of Xiaoyi County, Shanxi. He was an Assistant Commander serving as Commandant at Huai'an and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zishen; he ranked first among his brothers and was eighteen years old, born on the twentieth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Puxing, his grandfather was Cong, and his father was Yu; his mother was née Cao. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fifteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Liang, registered in a civilian household in Jinhua County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhifu; he ranked twenty-sixth in the family birth order and was thirty years old, born on the tenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather Yang was a County Magistrate, posthumously appointed a Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his grandfather was Tao, and his father Ji was a student of the Directorate of Education. His mother was née Zhu. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Chong, and his younger brother was Xiang. He married a woman née Qian. He placed fifty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ying Mingfeng, registered in Xi’an County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shiming, he ranked tenth among his brothers and male cousins, and he was twenty-three, born on the twelfth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang’an, posthumously appointed Magistrate; his grandfather was Neng, an Assistant Prefect who received successive promotions in prestige rank to Grand Master for Court Service (chaolie dafu); his father was Xu, a Director of Foodstuffs; his mother was née Chen, and his stepmother née Zheng. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Xiangfeng and Yifeng, and his wife was née Xu. He placed forty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Heng, registered in Wan’an County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shinan, he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, and he was twenty-one, born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zugui, an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions; his grandfather was Chong; his father was Peng, a sheren granted the privilege of wearing official cap and belt; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Sa [?], Long, Hang, Shun, Chong, and Fen, and his wife was née Liu. He placed ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Weixian, registered in Zhongjiang County, Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Shiguan, he ranked third among his brothers and male cousins, and he was twenty-seven, born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong, an Imperial University student; his grandfather was Pu; his father was Xi, an Imperial University student; and his mother was née Xia. Both parents were living; his elder brothers were Xixian and Jiexian, his younger brothers were Qingxian, Yixian, Yongxian, Jixian, Zaixian, Kuangxian, Chengxian, and Kexian, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed tenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Zhao, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shuchu, he ranked 138th among his brothers and male cousins, and he was thirty-one, born on the fourteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huan, his grandfather Shen, his father Shi, and his mother née Lin. Both parents were living; his elder brothers were Xiu and Xun, his younger brothers were Zheng, Fen, Ru, and Ao, and his wife was née Chen. He placed thirty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Feng Yingyuan, courtesy name Tiqian, was registered in an artisan household in Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather, Xi; and his father, Bin, a Food Steward. His mother was née Li. His mother alone survived. His younger brothers were Yingkui and Yingdeng, and his wife was née Lu. He placed forty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Deng, courtesy name Zixian, was registered in a military household in Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty-eight, born on the eighth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming; his grandfather, Jing; and his father, Jin. His mother was née Yao, and his stepmother was née Wang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Fa, Ji, and Cha [?], and his wife was née He. He placed fourteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Minshun, courtesy name Jingru, was registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in family order and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zixian; his grandfather, Qi, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; and his father, Yang, a County School Instructor. His father’s former wife was née Wu, his mother was née Zhang, and his stepmother was née Zeng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Minyi, a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Minshi, Minhuai, Minzhan, and Minxian. His wife was née Zhang. He placed thirty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xing Zhi, courtesy name Ruli, was registered in a military household in Dangtu County, Taiping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked eighth in family order and was aged thirty-nine, born on the ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun; his grandfather, Yu, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice; and his father, Xun, a Left Provincial Administration Commissioner. His mother was née Yang, granted the title of Lady of Peace, and his stepmother was née Ni. His father alone survived. His elder brothers were Zeng, Xun, Yin, Qi, Tan, Bi, Ai, Zhi, Yu, and Beng; his younger brothers were Fang, Yao, and Zhuang. His wife was née Xu. He placed fourteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hong Yuan, registered in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Junzhi. He ranked third in his family and was twenty-eight years old, born on the fifteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Liu, his father Hui, and his mother née Yu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Kun and Jun, and his younger brothers Gui, Qi, and Xun. His wife was née Hu. He placed one hundredth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Dalian, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jiefu. He ranked third in his family and was thirty-five years old, born on the twelfth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chaoyu, his grandfather Bosheng, and his father Zixun, Vice Commissioner of a Granary; his mother was née Zeng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Dazhong and Daxiao. His wife was née Lin. He placed third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chun, registered in Puzhou, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Wenqing. He ranked second in his family and was forty-four years old, born on the eighteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Cheng, and his father Zan, an honorary official for public service; his mother was née Ma. His parents were deceased. His elder brother Xun was a sacrificial official (shengjiguan). His wife was née Ren. He placed fourteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and two hundred twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Tianshou, registered in Wan’an County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Kequan. He ranked first in his family and was thirty-nine years old, born on the twentieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shanqing, a Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather was Xian, his father Qi, and his mother née Guo. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Tianqiu, and his younger brothers Tianzhi and Tianjian. His wife was née Zhou. He placed forty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and one hundred twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hu Yongtong, courtesy name Yiguan, was registered in a civilian household in Cao County, Cao Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Lun; his grandfather was Cong, an honorary official for public benefaction; his father was Guoan, an Assistant Prefect; and his mother was née Chen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Yongshou and Yongcheng, and his wife was née Li. He ranked forty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xun, courtesy name Shimin, was registered in a military household of Gaoyou Guard in Zhili. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather was Kai; his father was Yong, an honorary official recognized for longevity; and his mother was née Xuan. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Dao, a seventh-rank prestige official, and Xuan; his younger brothers were Zun and Kui. His wife was née Bai. He ranked 120th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 302nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Jixian, courtesy name Xiaoqing, was registered in a military household in Anyi County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the sixth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Duo; his grandfather was Cheng; his father was Wei; and his mother was née Ma. Both his parents were deceased. His elder brother was Lixue, and his younger brother was Xiaoxian. His first wife was née Song, and his subsequent wife was née Chen. He ranked fifty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Yu, courtesy name Liangqing, was registered in a civilian household in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was sixth in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the fourteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Hui; his grandfather was Jun; his father was Yunzhong, a student of the Imperial University; and his mother was née Zhu. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brother was Huang, and his younger brother was Xun. His wife was née Qian. He ranked fifty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Guangxun, registered in a civilian household in Xinchang County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xinqing; he ranked nineteenth in his family and was twenty-five years old, born on the seventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Haohe, his grandfather Ting’an, his father Shiliang, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Guangyan and Guangmi, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed twenty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Hao, registered in a civilian household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhixing; he ranked fourth in his family and was thirty-four years old, born on the nineteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Hongwei; his grandfather Delong was a provincial graduate (juren) and Acting Instructor, successively granted posthumous honors culminating in Director in the Ministry of Revenue. His father Tan was a Prefect granted an increased salary at the third rank, and his mother, née Li, was ennobled as Lady of Peace. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Yuzhang, a Magistrate, Yuqing, and Zhimin; his younger brothers were Yanchong and Wan. His wife was née Li. He placed thirty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Yue, registered in an artisan household under the Nanjing Embroidered-uniform Guard and a native of Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhongfu; he ranked second in his family and was thirty-one years old, born on the eighth day of the intercalary seventh month. His great-grandfather Xin held honorary office for longevity; his grandfather was Su, his father Qi, his father’s former wife née Li, and his mother née Wu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Chao, his younger brother Qi, and his wife was née Fang. He placed 125th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shi, registered in an official household under the Zhuolu Central Guard in the directly administered region and a native of Changle County, Fujian, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Yizhi; he ranked fourth in his family and was forty years old, born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather Tong was granted the honorary title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his father Yu was a Prefect; and his mother, née Wang, was ennobled as Lady of Suitability. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Wei, Yang, and Shou; his younger brother Jue was a Guard Pacification Officer. His wife was née Wang. He placed twentieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

孫簡〔貫直隸瀋陽中屯衛軍籍，山東招遠縣人，河間府學增廣生，治詩經，字維敬，行一，年三十一，六月十五日生〕。曾祖昭，祖宗堯〔通判〕，父復初〔甲戌進士〕，母張氏。慈侍下，兄厚，弟黙、高、遠、深、邃、宬，娶鄭氏。順天府鄉試第四名，會試第一百七名。

錢嶫〔貫直隸揚州府通州軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字君望，行一，年三十三，三月二十三日生〕。曾祖思禎，祖叔惠，父錄〔縣丞〕，母徐氏。嚴侍下，弟岎、𡶶、峘、峻、嶨、巍，娶曹氏，繼聘袁氏。應天府鄉試第七十九名，會試第二百五十六名。
translation_en:
Xie Jiuyi 謝九儀, courtesy name Junci, was registered in a civilian household in Zhangqiu County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third in his family and was thirty-two years old, born on the fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Song; his grandfather, Yu, was posthumously appointed Registrar of a guard; and his father, Suzhi, was Vice Commissioner of a Salt Distribution Commission, advanced to the rank of Grand Master for Deliberation. His mother, née Li, held the title Lady. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Jiuding, a Ceremonial Usher; Jiushao; and Jiuxu, a tribute scholar. His younger brothers were Jiushi and Jiuji. He married a woman née Xu. He placed thirty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Xiang 尹相, courtesy name Shangheng, was registered in a civilian household in Jiayu County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third in his family and was thirty-five years old, born on the third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fushao, his grandfather Youxian, and his father Dezhang; his mother was née Kong. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jing and Lun, and his younger brothers were Pu, Bin, Dong, and Mei. He married a woman née Lai. He placed twelfth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and three hundred eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Jian 孫簡, courtesy name Weijing, was registered in a military household in the Shenyang Central Garrison Guard in Zhili and was a native of Zhaoyuan County, Shandong. An additional student at the Hejian prefectural government school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in his family and was thirty-one years old, born on the fifteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhao; his grandfather, Zongyao, was an Assistant Prefect; and his father, Fuchu, was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the jiaxu year. His mother was née Zhang. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Hou, and his younger brothers were Mo, Gao, Yuan, Shen, Sui, and Cheng. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Ye 錢嶫, courtesy name Junwang, was registered in a military household in Tongzhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, Zhili. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in his family and was thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sizhen, his grandfather Shuhui, and his father Lu, a Vice Magistrate; his mother was née Xu. His father alone was living. His younger brothers were Fen, Feng, Huan, Jun, Xue, and Wei. He married a woman née Cao and was subsequently betrothed to a woman née Yuan. He placed seventy-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

何中行〔貫廣東廣州府順德縣民籍，南海縣人，國子生，治禮記，字粹甫，行三，年三十六，十二月二十七日生〕。曾祖源深，祖道養，父楚，母羅氏。具慶下，弟中淳、中立、中孚，娶羅氏。廣東鄉試第二十一名，會試第二百五十名。

吕應祥〔貫陝西西安府涇陽縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字子和，行一，年四十你，八月二十二日生〕。曾祖恭，祖勉，父誠〔衞經歷〕，母姚氏。慈侍下，弟應禄、應福，娶栢氏。陝西鄉試第四名，會試第一百二十二名。
translation_en:
Wu Boheng 吳伯亨, courtesy name Zizhen, was from Lanzhou, Lintao Prefecture, Shaanxi, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Shan, and his father Rui; his father's principal wife was née Shi, his birth mother née Wang, and his stepmother also née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Boxiang and Bolu. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently women née Han and née Ren. He ranked eighteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Ti 吳悌, courtesy name Sicheng, was registered in an artisan household in Jinxi County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and born on the second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shaoxian, his grandfather Fulin, his father Wang, and his mother née Zhu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yi and Yue. He married a woman née Che. He ranked forty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Zhongxing 何中行, courtesy name Cuifu, was registered in a civilian household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and was originally from Nanhai County. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanshen, his grandfather Daoyang, his father Chu, and his mother née Luo. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhongchun, Zhongli, and Zhongfu. He married a woman née Luo. He ranked twenty-first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Yingxiang 吕應祥, courtesy name Zihe, was registered in a military household in Jingyang County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. First in birth order, he was aged forty [?] and born on the twenty-second day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gong, his grandfather Mian, his father Cheng (a guard command's Office Manager), and his mother née Yao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Yinglu and Yingfu. He married a woman née Bai. He ranked fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 122nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Guangwen, courtesy name Jichun, was registered in a civilian household in Langzhong County, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan. A county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first in birth order and was twenty-six years old, born on the second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shen; his grandfather, Fen; and his father, Zhang, held an honorary longevity title. His father's principal wife was née Pu, and his birth mother was née Cheng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Guangchan, Guangguo, Guangren, Guangyi, Guangzhi, Guang'en, and Guanglai; his younger brothers were Guangqian, Guangwei, Guangye, Guangnian, and Pang [?]. His wife was née Wang. He placed forty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bao Jie, courtesy name Yuanda, was registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; his ancestral home was Jiaxing County, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Record of Rites, he ranked ninth in birth order and was twenty-seven years old, born on the sixteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Jun, was honorifically granted the title of Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites; his grandfather, Ding, was a Prefect, advanced to the prestige title of Grand Master of the Second Order (Yazhong dafu); and his father, Zhi, was an Imperial University student. His mother was née Yang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Hong, Hao, Yong, Chun, Lian, and Han; his younger brothers were Shen, Jie, Xiao (a tribute scholar), Bian, Su, Qia, and Ze. His wife was née Li. He placed twentieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 265th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Yingliang, courtesy name Xizai, was registered in a civilian household in Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An Imperial University student specializing in the Record of Rites, he ranked first in birth order and was twenty-seven years old, born on the tenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shiheng; his grandfather, Ruhe, was honorifically granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father, Chunze, was a Vice Prefect. His mother, née Chen, was granted the title of Lady of Peace (Anren). Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yingyan, and his wife was née Zheng. He placed sixty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ti, courtesy name Zijie, was registered in a military household in Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked fourth in birth order and was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong; his grandfather, Chen, held an honorary longevity title; and his father, Bo, was a county school Instructor. His mother was née Jia. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Kai, Qi, Tang, Xiu, Cai, Qu, Li, and Zhai; his younger brothers were Qing and Nan. His wife was née Wang. He placed fifty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.
