translation_en:
Gao Shangzhi, courtesy name Dechong, was registered in Guan County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household. An additional student of the county Confucian school, he specialized in the Book of Changes; he ranked first in birth order, was aged twenty-one, and was born on the fourth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was An, his grandfather Mian, and his father Tai; his father's principal wife was née Hou, and his birth mother was née Meng. His father was deceased, and he served his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Xiu, Lu, and Yu, and his younger brothers Shangyi, Shangzhi 尚質, and Shangbin. His wife was née Su. He placed seventeenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Kuan, courtesy name Lifu, was registered in Dantu County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a military artisan household. A student of the prefectural Confucian school, he specialized in the Book of Odes; he ranked sixth in birth order, was aged forty, and was born on the thirtieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Zhen, a seventh-rank prestige official, and his father Jizong, an honorary official recognized for public benefactions. His father's former wife was née Gu, his mother née Meng, and his stepmother née Zhao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xian, Shi, and Cha, and his younger brothers Rong, Wan, You, Chen, Jun, and Chong. His wife was née Qian. He placed forty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Guohua, courtesy name Shangbin, was registered in Xingguo Subprefecture, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sigong, his grandfather Xian, and his father Cong, an Instructor; his mother was née Zhong, and his stepmother née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Wenhua, Shihua, and Changhua. His wife was née Guo. He placed forty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Wenhao, courtesy name Zichuan, was registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. A student of the county Confucian school, he specialized in the Book of Changes; he ranked third in birth order, was aged forty-six, and was born on the twelfth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Bing, and his father Kuang; his father's former wife was née Wu, and his mother née Zheng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Wenyuan. His wife was née Dai. He placed forty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 297th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Rong, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Renqing, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the eighteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Kun, his grandfather Yuan, and his father Yu; his father's principal wife was née Wu, and his birth mother was née Lin. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jun and Guo, his younger brother was Gai, and his wife was née Zhang. He ranked fifty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Liang, registered in Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to an artisan household and was School Instructor at the Pizhou subprefectural school in the directly administered metropolitan region; he specialized in the Book of Changes, his courtesy name was Shangyin, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged forty-one, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Rong, a School Instructor; his grandfather was Yi'e, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his father was Tianzhi, his mother née Zhang, and his stepmother née Zhao. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Hao, Gao, and Heng, and his wife was née Wei. He ranked thirty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 126th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Tianmin, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Ruoyin, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the twelfth day of the intercalary third month. His great-grandfather was Kelü, his grandfather Yong, a Vice Commissioner of a granary, and his father Shiyong; his mother was née Zhan and his stepmother née Lin. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Tianjue, Tiancheng, and Tianqiu, and his wife was née Lin. He ranked thirty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Rutan, registered in Zhangping County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Weixin, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Chu'an, his grandfather Lan, an honorary official recognized for charitable service, and his father Yuanqing, an Administrative Clerk in a Provincial Surveillance Commission; his mother was née Chen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living, and his wife was née Yang. He ranked ninety-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

郭鋆〔貫山西澤州高平縣，民籍，國子生，治《春秋》，字允重，行一，年三十五，十月初八日生〕。曾祖質〔知州〕，祖定〔知州〕，父坤〔知州〕，母王氏。慈侍下，兄鑾〔貢士〕，弟釜、盤〔貢士〕、鑒、金、鎣、鎏。娶劉氏，繼娶邢氏。山西鄉試第五名，會試第四名。

杜銓〔貫浙江寧波府鄞縣，民籍，國子生，治《易經》，字邦平，行十四，年二十六，閏正月十九日生〕。曾祖允，祖儀，父璵，母董氏。具慶下，弟銳、銶、鍇、銈、鉉。娶徐氏。浙江鄉試第六十九名，會試第二百六十三名。

勞紹科〔貫廣東廣州府番禺縣，軍籍，國子生，治《詩經》，字獻伯，行一，年三十一，十月三十日生〕。曾祖秉貴，祖金悌，父琮，母陳氏。具慶下，弟紹學。娶翁氏。廣東鄉試第三十五名，會試第二百四十七名。

黃獻可〔貫福建興化府莆田縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治《詩經》，字尭俞，行四，年三十二，九月十四日生〕。曾祖孟恭，祖汝保，父思達，母林氏。具慶下，弟際可、學可。娶阮氏。福建鄉試第六十九名，會試第一百六十名。
translation_en:
Guo Yun, courtesy name Yunzhong, was registered in Gaoping County, Zezhou, Shanxi, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first in family birth order and was aged thirty-five, born on the eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhi, grandfather Ding, and father Kun were all department magistrates; his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Luan, a tribute student (gongshi); his younger brothers were Fu, Pan (a tribute student), Jian, Jin, Ying, and Liu. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Xing. He placed fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Quan, courtesy name Bangping, was registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fourteenth in family birth order and was aged twenty-six, born on the nineteenth day of the intercalary first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yun, his grandfather Yi, his father Yu, and his mother née Dong. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Rui, Qiu, Kai, Ji, and Xuan. He married a woman née Xu. He placed sixty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lao Shaoke, courtesy name Xianbo, was registered in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in family birth order and was aged thirty-one, born on the thirtieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Binggui, his grandfather Jinti, his father Cong, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Shaoxue. He married a woman née Weng. He placed thirty-fifth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Xianke, courtesy name Yaoyu, was registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth in family birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Menggong, his grandfather Rubao, his father Sida, and his mother née Lin. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jike and Xueke. He married a woman née Ruan. He placed sixty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 160th in the Metropolitan Examination.

路天亨〔貫山西平陽府安邑縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字仲元，行二，年三十一，九月三十日生〕。曾祖廣〔義官〕，祖顯〔知縣〕，父塤〔典膳〕，母楊氏。具慶下，兄天衢〔監生〕。娶張氏，繼娶景氏。山西鄉試第二十六名，會試第一百六十七名。

張光祖〔貫河南潁川衛，軍籍，山西陽曲縣人，國子生，治詩經，字德徵，行一，年二十八，二月十六日生〕。曾祖珣，祖守亨〔知縣〕，父治〔貢士〕，母李氏。具慶下，弟光遠、光弼、光祚、光大、光國、光啓、光裕、光緒、光世。娶時氏。河南鄉試第二十五名，會試第二百二十八名。

陶謨〔貫浙江嘉興府秀水縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字大顯，行一，年三十七，二月十三日生〕。曾祖澤〔義官〕，祖楷〔義官，贈監察御史〕，父儼〔按察司副使〕，母姜氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下，弟諾、託〔監生〕、誥、訥、試、誼、訓。娶李氏。浙江鄉試第二十九名，會試第一百二十名。

劉九容〔貫陝西綏德衛，官籍，榆林衛人，國子生，治春秋，字慎卿，行二，年三十六，四月初五日生〕。曾祖釗，祖頊〔義官〕，父儒，母楊氏。慈侍下，兄九思。娶吳氏。陝西鄉試第二十名，會試第二百五十四名。
translation_en:
Lu Tianheng, courtesy name Zhongyuan, was registered in a commoner household in Anyi County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the thirtieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guang, an honorary official recognized for public benefactions; his grandfather was Xian, a Magistrate; his father was Xun, a Director of Catering; and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Tianqu, was an Imperial University student. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Jing. He ranked twenty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Guangzu, courtesy name Dezheng, was registered in a military household of Yingchuan Guard, Henan, and was originally from Yangqu County, Shanxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the sixteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xun; his grandfather was Shouheng, a Magistrate; his father was Zhi, a tribute scholar (gongshi); and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Guangyuan, Guangbi, Guangzuo, Guangda, Guangguo, Guangqi, Guangyu, Guangxu, and Guangshi. He married a woman née Shi. He ranked twenty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tao Mo, courtesy name Daxian, was registered in a military household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the thirteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ze, an honorary official recognized for public benefactions; his grandfather was Kai, likewise an honorary official, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; his father was Yan, a Vice Commissioner of the Provincial Surveillance Commission; and his mother was née Jiang, granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Nuo, Tuo (an Imperial University student), Gao, Ne, Shi, Yi, and Xun. He married a woman née Li. He ranked twenty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 120th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Jiurong, courtesy name Shenqing, was registered in an official household of Suide Guard, Shaanxi, and was originally from Yulin Guard. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhao; his grandfather was Xu, an honorary official recognized for public benefactions; his father was Ru; and his mother was née Yang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Jiusi. He married a woman née Wu. He ranked twentieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 254th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jia Wenyuan, registered in a military household of Dali Guard, Yunnan, was originally from Quyang County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Tiren, ranked third in family seniority, and was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shun, his grandfather Neng, his father Duo, and his mother Lady Wei; both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wenying, Wenhan (Superintendent), Wenfu, and Wenhua; his younger brother was Wenkui. He married Lady Zhu and subsequently Lady Su. He placed twentieth in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Xun, registered in a military household of Jinyun County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruli; he ranked thirty-seventh in family seniority and was aged forty, born on the twenty-third day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shouyi (honored as a Righteous Commoner), his grandfather Shixi, his father Shimian (an official holding a prestige title), and his mother Lady Ying; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhu, Yao, Fan [?], Lian, Jie, Dao, and Dian (a tribute scholar); his younger brothers were Yi and Tun. He married Lady Jiang. He placed fifty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yingzhao, registered in a civilian household of Ouning County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Gongju; he ranked fourth in family seniority and was aged forty-three, born on the fourteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Minzhan, his father Gui (an annual tribute student), and his mother Lady Wei; both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Menbin, and his younger brother Shice (a tribute scholar). He married Lady Lei. He placed eighteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 303rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Rulian, registered in a civilian household of Taihe County, Dali Prefecture, Yunnan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Dunfu; he ranked first in family seniority and was aged thirty-eight, born on the thirtieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Ping (posthumously appointed Judicial Officer of Yingtian Prefecture), his father Yi (a Department Magistrate), and his mother Lady Duan (granted the title Lady of Repose); both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Ruluo. He married Lady Yao and subsequently Lady Wang. He placed third in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

薛廷寵〔貫福建福州府福清縣，軍鹽籍，國子生，治詩經，字汝承，行八，年二十五，三月十五日生。〕曾祖世暉，祖尚脩，父德佐，母華氏，繼母李氏。慈侍下，弟廷賓、廷亮，娶鄭氏，繼娶蒲氏。福建鄉試第三十六名，會試第一百十六名。

史褒善〔貫直隸大名府開州，民籍，國子生，治易經，字文直，行一，年三十四，十二月初十日生。〕曾祖敬，祖英，父記，前母王氏，母馬氏，繼母孫氏。嚴侍下，弟揚善、旌善，娶張氏。順天府鄉試第二百一名，會試第二百四十三名。
translation_en:
Bian Hang 邊沆, courtesy name Wenhao, was from Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, with official household registration; a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in his family, was aged twenty-three, and was born on the ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather Quan and grandfather Hong were Company Commanders; his father was Ru and his mother was née Lü; his parents and at least one grandparent were living; his elder brothers were Shi, a Company Commander, and Cen, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year, his younger brothers were Wo and Cang, and his wife was née Yu; he placed thirty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Yongxiu 申用休, courtesy name Jiezhi, was from Leping County, Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, with military household registration; an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in his family, was aged forty, and was born on the seventeenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duo, his grandfather Xin, his father Lang, and his mother née Hao; his mother was living and his father deceased; his younger brothers were Yongmao and Yongzhang, and he married a woman née Guo and subsequently a woman née Li; he placed sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 220th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Tingchong 薛廷寵, courtesy name Rucheng, was from Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, with military salt-producing household registration; an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked eighth in his family, was aged twenty-five, and was born on the fifteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shihui, his grandfather Shangxiu, his father Dezuo, his mother née Hua, and his stepmother née Li; his mother was living and his father deceased; his younger brothers were Tingbin and Tingliang, and he married a woman née Zheng and subsequently a woman née Pu; he placed thirty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 116th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Baoshan 史褒善, courtesy name Wenzhi, was from Kai Subprefecture, Daming Prefecture, Zhili, with civilian household registration; an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in his family, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Ying, and his father Ji; his father's former wife was née Wang, his mother was née Ma, and his stepmother was née Sun; his father was living and his mother deceased; his younger brothers were Yangshan and Jingshan, and his wife was née Zhang; he placed 201st in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

唐寬〔貫山西太原府平定州，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字栗夫，行二，年三十四，十二月二十九日生〕。曾祖謙，祖茂，父廷琰，母荆氏，繼母王氏。具慶下，兄寵，弟寀，娶黃氏。山西鄉試第五十五名，會試第一百四十八名。

姚虞〔貫福建興化府莆田縣，民籍，府學附學生，治詩經，字宗舜，行一，年二十六，九月十四日生〕。曾祖資德，祖商〔封南京太常寺博士〕，父鳴鸞〔知縣〕，母董氏。重慶下，弟夏、殷、周，娶林氏。福建鄉試第二十名，會試第二百三十六名。

楊賢〔貫山東兖州府濟寧州，民籍，國子生，治易經，字公薦，行二，年二十七，八月二十五日生〕。曾祖賓〔贈都察院右副都御史〕，祖汴〔散官〕，父粟〔訓導〕，母李氏。具慶下，兄貢，娶秦氏。山東鄉試第四十七名，會試第一百八十七名。

陳讓〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣，軍籍，府學生，治春秋，字原禮，行五，年四十二，十二月初五日生〕。曾祖漢，祖凱，父溥，嫡母莊氏，生母郭氏。永感下，兄言、詵、謀、試，娶李氏。福建鄉試第一名，會試第五十二名。
translation_en:
Tang Kuan, registered in Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Lifu. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-four and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qian, his grandfather Mao, and his father Tingyan; his mother was née Jing and his stepmother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chong and his younger brother Cai; his wife was née Huang. He ranked fifty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 148th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Yu, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zongshun. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-six and was born on the fourteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zide, his grandfather Shang (honorarily appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in Nanjing), and his father Mingluan (a District Magistrate); his mother was née Dong. Parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Xia, Yin, and Zhou; his wife was née Lin. He ranked twentieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Xian, registered in Jining Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Gongjian. Second in birth order, he was aged twenty-seven and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin (posthumously appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate), his grandfather Bian (an official with prestige rank), and his father Su (an Assistant Instructor); his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Gong; his wife was née Qin. He ranked forty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Rang, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Yuanli. Fifth in birth order, he was aged forty-two and was born on the fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Han, his grandfather Kai, and his father Pu; his father's principal wife was née Zhuang, and his birth mother was née Guo. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yan, Shen, Mou, and Shi; his wife was née Li. He ranked first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xie Shangzhen 謝上箴, courtesy name Yishan, was registered in a scholarly household in Huarong County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked thirteenth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged forty-seven, born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Chunyi; his grandfather, Wen; and his father, Rang, Office Manager in the Ministry of Rites at Nanjing. His father's principal wife was Lady Yuan, his stepmother Lady He, and his birth mother Lady Liu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Shangzuo, Shangyou, Shangnan, Shangfu, Shangce, and Shangxuan; his younger brothers were Shangjian and Shangpian. He married Lady Liu. He placed fifty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Tingchen 朱廷臣, courtesy name Jingzhi, was registered in a commoner household in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was aged forty, born on the twelfth day of the intercalary fifth month. His great-grandfather was Hui; his grandfather, You; his father, Lu; and his mother, Lady You. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Tingyu, Tingpu, Tingxuan, Tingfu, and Tingzuo. He married Lady Gui and subsequently Lady Zheng. He placed twenty-ninth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Yu 董玙, courtesy name Zichun, was registered in a military household in Jing County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked eighty-fourth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-six, born on the sixth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhidao, an honorary official who received successive posthumous honors culminating in the title of Prefect; his grandfather was Jie, Right Vice Censor-in-chief; his father was Jian; and his mother, Lady Xu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Qiu and Lin; his younger brothers were Zhen, Jin, and Xiu. He married Lady Zuo. He placed 122nd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Zi 楊鎡, courtesy name Yingshi, was registered in a bannerman household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Huguan County, Shanxi. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-seven, born on the fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Tong, posthumously granted the title of Assistant Commander; his grandfather, Qing, and his father, Shen, were honorary officials. His father's principal wife was Lady Tong, and his birth mother was Lady Gu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Yue; his younger brothers were Keng and Huang. He married Lady Liu and subsequently Lady Zhang. He placed forty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Shou, courtesy name Rujing, was registered in an artisan household in Wanping County, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a native of Yichuan County, Shaanxi. An additional-quota student of the Shuntian prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Documents; he was fourth in family order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the seventeenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wengui, his grandfather Xing, and his father Ao; his father’s former wife was née Guo, his legal mother née Wu, and his birth mother née Zhao. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Fu, Lu, and Jue (an honorary official). He married a woman née Yu. He ranked ninety-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Yunheng, courtesy name Botong, was registered in a military household in Ansu County, Baoding Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region. A county-school student, he specialized in the Book of Changes; he was seventh in family order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the thirteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Zong, his father Tingyi, and his mother née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yungong, Yundao, Yunzhong, Yundi, Yungao, and Yunhuai; his younger brother was Yunxiu. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Liu. He ranked 101st in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tao Qinkui, courtesy name Boxie, was registered in a civilian household in Pengze County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents; he was ninth in family order, aged thirty, and born on the fourth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather Zhuo and father Ye were both medical instructors. His mother was née Song and his stepmother née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qinmin (a tribute scholar) and Qinshi (a medical student); his younger brothers were Qinzhong (a student of the Directorate of Education) and Qingao. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née Bi. He ranked forty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 173rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Yong, courtesy name Shouqing, was registered in a civilian household in Wei County, Guangping Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes; he was fifth in family order, aged thirty-one, and born on the seventh day of the intercalary seventh month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Rong, his father Jian, and his mother née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. He married a woman née Sun. He ranked 107th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Shixian, registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yidao; he ranked first among his brothers, was forty-five years old, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiesheng; his grandfather was Bogong, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his father was Tingzhong, a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works; and his mother, née Wang, was granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren). His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Shigui, a Clerk in a Guard, Shizi, and Shizan. He married a woman née Xiong and subsequently married women née Tang and née Ge. He placed fifty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Gui, registered in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Junru; he ranked third among his brothers, was thirty-seven years old, and was born on the twenty-second day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanpeng, his grandfather Qin, and his father Xian; his mother was née Lu, and his stepmother was née Zhou. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers are listed as Luan, Yuan, Bi, Yue, and Qiu. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed thirty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Nan, registered in Jia County, Ruzhou Subprefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Daonan; he ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-nine years old, and was born on the eighteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huang, his grandfather Rong, and his father Qi; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Shen. He placed fifty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xianzhi, registered in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Deren; he ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-three years old, and was born on the thirtieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongliang; his grandfather was Ai, granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his father was Chong, a Subprefectural Vice Magistrate; and his mother, née Fang, was granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren). His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Xiankui and Xianjin. He married a woman née Yu. He placed fifteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

董德明〔貫廣西護衛中所軍籍，湖廣黃岡縣人，國子生，治禮記，字汝哲，行七，年二十七，十月初三日生〕。曾祖繼宗，祖春，父勉〔義官〕，母郭氏。重慶下，兄德順、德純〔教諭〕、德茂，弟德潤、德宏、德昇，娶劉氏。廣西鄉試第四名，會試第三百六名。
translation_en:
Sun Jiao 孫校, courtesy name Youwen, was registered in a civilian household in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, and was second in birth order, born on the fourteenth day of the eighth month (the preceding birth or age wording is defective [?]). His great-grandfather was Tao, posthumously or honorifically appointed Magistrate; his grandfather was Kui; his father was Shou, a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Zhou. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Gai, a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Zhirong, also a student of the Directorate of Education, Shi, Ji, He, Zhu 祝, and Zhu 柱. He married a woman née Bao. He ranked twenty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hou Pei 侯珮, courtesy name Tianhe, was registered in a civilian household in Fan County, Pu Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, third in birth order, aged forty-five, and born on the fourteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Qin; his grandfather was Rong; his father was Cong, a Guard's Registrar; and his mother was née Zhai. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhang, Gui, and Fan, the last awaiting selection for official appointment. He married a woman née Cui. He ranked twenty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hou Du 侯度, courtesy name Xianfu, was registered in a military household in Dong'e County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong; he was a county government student specializing in the Book of Odes, third in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-third day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather was Guan, a tribute scholar; his father was Keyi; and his mother was née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Qing and Chen. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Li. He ranked forty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Deming 董德明, courtesy name Ruzhe, was registered in a military household of the Central Battalion of the Guangxi Princely Guard and was a native of Huanggang County, Huguang; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites, seventh in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the third day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Jizong; his grandfather was Chun; his father was Mian, an honorary official; and his mother was née Guo. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Deshun, Dechun, an Instructor, and Demao; his younger brothers were Derun, Dehong, and Desheng. He married a woman née Liu. He ranked fourth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 306th in the Metropolitan Examination.

汪東洋〔貫四川成都府綿州，民籍，國子生，治書經，字德涵，行一，年三十四，三月初六日生〕。曾祖思拳，祖志訓，父昌〔驛丞〕，嫡母何氏，生母陳氏。嚴侍下，弟東海、東瀛、東洲，娶李氏。四川鄉試第三十二名，會試第一百三名。

劉訓〔貫河南汝寧府汝陽縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治易經，字子伊，行二，年二十七，五月二十二日生〕。曾祖瑛〔布政司照磨，贈監察御史〕，祖紳〔按察司副使，詔進三品通議大夫〕，父繼儒〔監生〕，母彭氏。具慶下，兄誨，弟謨、訥、試、評、講、誦、讀、謐、詩，娶伍氏，繼娶樊氏。河南鄉試第二十九名，會試第一百九十四名。

劉士達〔貫浙江寧波府慈谿縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字伯鴻，行百七，年三十五，十一月十八日生〕。曾祖煒〔布政司左叅政〕，祖圻〔正七品承事郎〕，父鍇〔府經歷〕，前母桂氏、方氏，母汪氏。具慶下，弟士逢，娶王氏。浙江鄉試第四十二名，會試第八十一名。

何元述〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字元孝，行一，年二十九，十二月初二日生〕。曾祖貴易，祖燦〔典史〕，父雄，母柯氏。具慶下，兄綱〔學正〕、紀、元褒、元寀，弟元脩、元郁、元選，娶莊氏。福建鄉試第七十四名，會試第三百名。
translation_en:
Wang Dongyang 汪東洋, registered in Mianzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Dehan. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-four and was born on the sixth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Siquan; his grandfather was Zhixun; and his father was Chang, a Post Station Master. His legal mother was née He, and his birth mother was née Chen. His father was still living, his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Donghai, Dongying, and Dongzhou. He married a woman née Li. He ranked thirty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 103rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Xun 劉訓, registered in Ruyang County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziyi. Second in birth order, he was aged twenty-seven and was born on the twenty-second day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, a Records Keeper in a Provincial Administration Commission, posthumously appointed an Investigating Censor. His grandfather was Shen, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, promoted by imperial decree to the third-rank prestige title Grand Master for Thorough Counsel. His father was Jiru, a student of the Directorate of Education, and his mother was née Peng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Hui; his younger brothers were Mo 謨, Ne 訥, Shi 試, Ping 評, Jiang 講, Song 誦, Du 讀, Mi 謐, and Shi 詩. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Fan. He ranked twenty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Shida 劉士達, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Bohong. He stood 107th in the family birth-order sequence, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wei, a Left Administration Adviser in a Provincial Administration Commission. His grandfather was Qi, who held the prestige title Gentleman for Rendering Service, of the primary seventh rank. His father was Kai, a Prefectural Registrar. His father's former wives were née Gui and née Fang; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Shifeng. He married a woman née Wang. He ranked forty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Yuanshu 何元述, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yuanxiao. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guiyi; his grandfather was Can, a County Clerk; his father was Xiong; and his mother was née Ke. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Gang, a School Instructor, Ji, Yuanbao, and Yuancai; his younger brothers were Yuanxiu, Yuanyu, and Yuanxuan. He married a woman née Zhuang. He ranked seventy-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 300th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hu Ruyi, registered in a civilian household in Mianzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Bolin, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged forty-six, born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, posthumously granted the title Gentleman for Rendering Virtue; his grandfather was Lan, a Judicial Officer in a princely establishment; his father was Bingzhong, a Professor; his mother was née Gu and his stepmother née Li 栗. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ruxian, and his younger brothers were Rubi, Ruwei, Rulin, Ruji, and Rumei; his wife was née Li 李. He placed fifty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Dechun, registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Jingxiu, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the eleventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shangbin, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Yuanshen; his father was Xueshan; and his mother was née Jiang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Dezhao, and his wife was née Zhou. He placed ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Lin, registered in an official household of Dezhou Guard in the Metropolitan Region and originally from Jiangyin County, was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Maoqing, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather was Yu; his father was Qi; and his mother was née Song. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xiong, his younger brother was Yong, and his wife was née Yang. He placed fifteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Sitang, registered in a military household of Ningxia Right Guard in Shaanxi and originally from Xiangfu County, Henan, was a student of the guard school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shangyou, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi; his grandfather was San; his father was Xiong; and his mother was née Gan. Both parents were living, and his wife was née Guo. He placed twelfth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

閻樸〔貫山西太原府榆次縣，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字文甫，行二，年二十九，六月初九日生〕。曾祖最，祖瓚〔封主事〕，父大綸，母張氏，繼母李氏。具慶下，兄梅，弟模、桓、格、樞、梯，娶郝氏。山西鄉試第二名，會試第一百九十六名。

孫哲〔貫山西太原府石州，民籍，國子生，治易經，字用晦，行三，年三十九，十月十五日生〕。曾祖全〔壽官〕，祖撝〔教授〕，父子文〔知縣〕，前母蘇氏，母武氏。慈侍下，兄振麒〔大使〕、賢良，娶高氏，繼娶賈氏。山西鄉試第十四名，會試第六十六名。

胡守中〔貫河南開封府歸德州寧陵縣，軍籍，江西吉水縣人，國子生，治詩經，字伯時，行一，年三十一，四月初七日生〕。曾祖浩，祖暹〔壽官〕，父霽，母喬氏。嚴侍下，弟守正、守道、守義，娶趙氏，繼娶李氏。河南鄉試第七十一名，會試第一百三十九名。
translation_en:
Shen Hongyi, registered in a civilian household in Chenzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Junxu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty-two sui, born on the twenty-fourth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Cong, his grandfather Hao, and his father Ming, a tribute scholar; his mother was née Song, and both parents were living. His younger brothers were Honghua, Hong’en, and Hongze, and his wife was née Chen. He placed twentieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Pu, registered in a military household in Yuci County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Wenfu, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was twenty-nine sui, born on the ninth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zui, his grandfather Zan, who had been granted the title of Secretary, and his father Dalun; his mother was née Zhang and his stepmother née Li, and both parents were living. His elder brother was Mei and his younger brothers were Mo, Huan, Ge, Shu, and Ti; his wife was née Hao. He placed second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Zhe, registered in a civilian household in Shizhou, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yonghui, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was thirty-nine sui, born on the fifteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Quan, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Hui, a Prefectural School Instructor; and his father was Ziwen, a District Magistrate. His father’s former wife was née Su and his mother was née Wu; his mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Zhenqi, a Commissioner, and Xianliang; his wife was née Gao, and his subsequent wife was née Jia. He placed fourteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Shouzhong, registered in a military household in Ningling County, Guide Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, and originally from Jishui County, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Boshi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty-one sui, born on the seventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Hao, his grandfather Xian, an honorary official for longevity, and his father Ji; his mother was née Qiao, and his father alone was living. His younger brothers were Shouzheng, Shoudao, and Shouyi; his wife was née Zhao, and his subsequent wife was née Li. He placed seventy-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

田大有〔貫山東兖州府東平州，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字豫甫，行一，年二十九，九月初一日生〕。曾祖弘，祖安〔驛丞〕，父明〔義官〕，前母馬氏、屈氏，母徐氏。具慶下，弟大登、大豐、大範、大壯，娶李氏。山東鄉試第四十四名，會試第一百八十六名。

席大賓〔貫雲南雲南左衛，官籍，直隸定遠縣人，澂江府學生，治易經，字子瞻，行三，年三十四，五月二十日生〕。曾祖龐，祖允中〔壽官〕，父純〔監生〕，母向氏，繼母藺氏。具慶下，兄璋〔指揮僉事〕、尚賢，娶陳氏。雲貴鄉試第二十五名，會試第二百十一名。

李謹〔貫冨峪衛，官籍，廣東四會縣人，國子生，治書經，字常甫，行二，年四十一，正月初五日生〕。曾祖安〔百戶〕，祖福〔百戶〕，父淮〔百戶〕，母張氏〔封安人〕。永感下，兄讚〔百戶〕，弟諫〔義官〕，娶卞氏，繼聘何氏。順天府鄉試第一百十六名，會試第七十一名。

董官〔貫山西大同府應州，民籍，國子生，治易經，字惟賢，行一，年三十二，四月十二日生〕。曾祖政，祖銓〔縣主簿〕，父獻〔縣主簿〕，母鄭氏。具慶下，弟宇，娶李氏。山西鄉試第六十一名，會試第一百五名。
translation_en:
Tian Dayou, registered in a civilian household in Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Yufu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the first day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Hong; his grandfather, An, was a Postmaster; his father, Ming, held the honorary title of Official for Righteous Conduct; his father's former wives were née Ma and née Qu, and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Dadeng, Dafeng, Dafan, and Dazhuang, and his wife was née Li. He placed forty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xi Dabin, registered in an official household of the Yunnan Left Guard in Yunnan and originally from Dingyuan County in Zhili, was a student of the Chengjiang Prefectural School specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Zizhan, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the twentieth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Pang; his grandfather, Yunzhong, held the honorary title of Longevity Official; his father, Chun, was a student of the Directorate of Education; his mother was née Xiang, and his stepmother was née Lin. Both parents were living; his elder brothers were Zhang, an Assistant Commander, and Shangxian, and his wife was née Chen. He placed twenty-fifth in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jin, registered in an official household of Fuyu Guard and originally from Sihui County, Guangdong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Changfu, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged forty-one, born on the fifth day of the first month. His great-grandfather, An, his grandfather, Fu, and his father, Huai, were all Company Commanders; his mother, née Zhang, had been granted the title Lady of Peace. Both parents were deceased; his elder brother, Zan, was a Company Commander, and his younger brother, Jian, held the honorary title of Official for Righteous Conduct. He married a woman née Bian and was subsequently betrothed to a woman née He. He placed 116th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Guan, registered in a civilian household in Ying Subprefecture, Datong Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Weixian, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the twelfth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zheng; his grandfather, Quan, and his father, Xian, were County Registrars; his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were living; his younger brother was Yu, and his wife was née Li. He placed sixty-first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Shunchen, courtesy name Xigao, was registered in a civilian household in Anping County, Jinzhou Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the eleventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Kai; his grandfather, Lun, was a County Registrar; his father was Tianzhi; his mother was née Wang, and his stepmother née Liu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Yaochen and his younger brother Hanchen. He married a woman née Wang. He placed eighty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Gonglian, courtesy name Jieqing, was registered in a civilian household in Tangxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was eighth in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the sixteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yiying; his grandfather, Shigui, held an honorary official title for longevity; his father was Chang [悵; ?], and his mother née Dai. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Gongming and Gongshu. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed seventy-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Ji, courtesy name Ruzai, was registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the nineteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xun; his grandfather, Wenji, had been granted the privilege of wearing an official cap and girdle under applicable regulations; his father was Tingzuo, and his mother née Sun. Both his parents were living. His elder brothers were Jie and Ji; his younger brothers were Sheng, Ce, Zuan, Quan, Zhu, Chou, Fan, Jian, Pian, Zhen, and Fu. The annotation records that he married a woman née Xu and subsequently women née Gong and Ding. He placed ninety-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Ji, courtesy name Ruliang, was registered in a civilian household in Zhuji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the eighteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Maoying; his grandfather, Cong, held an honorary official title for longevity; his father, Fengqi, was a County School Instructor; and his mother was née Zheng. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Hua, Liu, and Qi; his younger brothers were Lai, Teng, Lu, Yuan, Si, Xiang, and Chi. He married a woman née Fu. He placed forty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zheng Pu 鄭普, courtesy name Rude, was registered in a military household in Nan’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian; he was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the nineteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Feiqi 妃乞 [?], his grandfather Mazan 媽讚 [?], his father Yuan, and his mother née Wu; both parents were living; his younger brothers were Zao, Jin, and Zhuang; he married a woman née Yang and ranked twenty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Ben 李本, courtesy name Ruli, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the first day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gongqiong, his grandfather Mao, and his father Gai; his father’s former wife was née Yu and his mother née Yang; his mother alone was living; his younger brothers were He, Du, Le, Cai, and Lai; he married a woman née Xia and ranked twenty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Weiyuan 趙維垣, courtesy name Boshi, was registered in an official household in Yongning Guard, Guizhou, and was originally from Jiangdu County in the directly administered metropolitan region; he was a guard school student specializing in the Book of Documents, second in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the thirtieth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Quan, and his father Di, an Honorary Official for Philanthropy; his mother was née Zhou and his stepmother née Wen; his mother alone was living; his elder brother was Weifan and his younger brothers Weiping, Weihan, and Weining; he married a woman née Xu and ranked fifty-first in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yi Minsheng 伊敏生, courtesy name Zimeng, was registered in an artisan household in Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was originally from Wu County in the directly administered metropolitan region; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, third in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the first day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pu, granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather Cheng was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, and his father Boxiong a Vice Prefect; his father’s former wife was née Zhou and his mother née Fu; both parents were living; his elder brothers were Dasheng and Zhisheng and his younger brother Lusheng; he married a woman née Ye and ranked twenty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

呂懷健〔貫錦衣衛軍籍，直隸揚州府泰州人，國子生，治《詩經》，字思順，行三，年三十四，七月十一日生〕。曾祖清，祖洪〔序班，贈刑部郎中〕，父傑〔知府〕，前母陳氏〔贈宜人〕，母馬氏〔封宜人〕。慈侍下，兄懷秀，弟懷德，娶唐氏。順天府鄉試第九十一名，會試第二百五十三名。

陳諫〔貫廣東廣州府番禺縣軍籍，順德縣人，國子生，治《詩經》，字公從，行一，年三十五，十二月初八日生〕。曾祖濶，祖瓊，父紀，母劉氏。具慶下，弟謨、詵、試，娶林氏。廣東鄉試第二十五名，會試第二百三十名。
translation_en:
Li Wan, courtesy name Zimei, was registered in a civilian household in Shishou County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the fourteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Maozhen; his grandfather, Deliang, was a District Magistrate; his father was Tianhe, and his mother was née Yuan. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shi, and his younger brothers were Rong, Guan, and Shou. His wife was née Zhang. He placed thirtieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Huaigan, courtesy name Shouzheng, was registered in an artisan household in Gui’an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked eighth among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the twenty-seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather, Tingli, held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather was Zhang; his father was Yuan, and his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Huaizhen, and his younger brothers were Huaizhong, Huaice, Huailiang, Huaicai, and Huairong. His wife was née Wu; his subsequent wife was née Min. He placed twelfth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 304th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Huaijian, courtesy name Sishun, was registered in a military household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Taizhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the eleventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather, Hong, was an Usher, posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father, Jie, was a Prefect. His father’s former wife, née Chen, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Suitability; his mother, née Ma, was granted the same title. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Huaixiu, and his younger brother was Huaide. His wife was née Tang. He placed ninety-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Jian, courtesy name Gongcong, was registered in a military household in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and was a native of Shunde County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kuo; his grandfather was Qiong; his father was Ji, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Mo, Shen, and Shi. His wife was née Lin. He placed twenty-fifth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Jifang 王繼芳, courtesy name Shichang, was registered in a civilian household in Gu’an County, Shuntian Prefecture. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-nine years old, born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather, Duan, was posthumously appointed Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Justice; and his father, Qin, was Vice Commissioner of a Provincial Surveillance Commission. His father’s former wife, née Lü, was posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren), and his mother, née Zu, was granted the same title. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Chen. He placed 107th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 162nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shixi 陳時熈, courtesy name Shunmin, was registered in a military household in Shangcai County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, and was originally from Chenliu County, Kaifeng Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked ninth among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the seventh day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Su; his grandfather was An; and his father, Zhiwen, was a Prefectural Vice Prefect, successively promoted to the ranks of Grand Master for Discussion and Administrator for Assisting Governance. His father’s former wife was née Yang, and his mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Song, Xu, Yong, Yun, Xian, Yu, and Shiyong; his younger brother was Shihao. He married a woman née Zheng and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed thirty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chaoxian 王朝賢, courtesy name Lizhi, was registered in a civilian household in Taikang County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zan; his grandfather was Tao; his father was Zai; and his mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Chaoyuan, and his wife was née Li. He placed twenty-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 317th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Zhaonan 方召南, courtesy name Wenhua, was registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the second month. His great-grandfather, Xuan, was an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather was Di; his father was Shen; and his mother was née Lin. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Shinan and Daonan. He married a woman née Zheng and subsequently another woman née Zheng. He placed ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 316th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
He Zan, registered in Huangyan County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yaoqing, he ranked ninth among his brothers, and he was aged forty, born on the twenty-first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shizhou, his grandfather Tan, and his father Gui; his father's former wife was née Xie, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Jin, and his younger brothers were Yin, Zhao, Yue, and Qiu. His wife was née Qiu. He placed seventy-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Xianzhang, registered in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shouliang, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guangfu, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Qiming, his father Kui, and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yizhang, Kuizhang, Chengzhang, Fengzhang, Baozhang, and Shizhang. His wife was née Yu. He placed thirteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Hongdao, registered in Zhanhua County, Binzhou Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shida, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Feng, and his father Qing, an honorary official for philanthropy; his mother was née Sun. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Hongren, and his wife was née Su. He placed eleventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and three hundred fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Mianxue, registered in Chiping County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a county government student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Zhongqian, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged forty-one, born on the ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather was Jing, a County Vice Magistrate; and his father was Chun, a student of the Directorate of Education. His father's former wife was née Ding, and his mother was née Tian. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Xixue, a County Magistrate. His wife was née Li, and his subsequent wife was née Zhao. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fan Ai, registered in a military household of the Yingzhou Central Garrison Guard under the Daning Regional Military Commission and a native of Wenshang County, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tiren; he ranked second in birth order and was aged thirty-three, born on the first day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Qing, and his father Shan; his mother was née Yuan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Zhang and his younger brother Chun; his wife was née Gong. He placed 126th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 301st in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Cheng, registered in an officer household of Suide Guard, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shufang; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-three, born on the seventeenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather Hong and grandfather Ying were both Pacification Officers; his father Xuan was a Battalion Commander. His father's former wives were née Zhao and née Wen, his legal mother was née Liu, and his birth mother was née Yang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother Tang was an Associate Commander; his younger brothers were Jian, Ji, Zhi, Zeng, Kun, and Dian. His wife was née Zhu. He placed 61st in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ran Chongli, registered in a military household of Zhongmou County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jizhou; he ranked third in birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Ming, his grandfather Yi, and his father Ding, a District Magistrate; his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chongru, a District Magistrate, and Chongshi; his younger brother was Chongxin. His wife was née Wang. He placed 64th in the Henan Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Biao, registered in a civilian household of Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhengfu; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twelfth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Ti, his grandfather Shanghui, and his father Hai; his mother was née Lin. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xiang, Luo, and Zhong; his wife was née Chen. He placed 36th in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hu Mingshu 胡明庶, registered in Luotian County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Gongfu; he ranked tenth in family order, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Zong and grandfather Yuehui held honorary offices for longevity; his father Daji held an honorary office for righteousness. His father’s former wife was Lady Wang, and his mother was Lady Xu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Mingru, a National University student; Mingzhe, an honorary official for righteousness; Mingzhong, an Adjudicator; Mingshan, whose annotation reads “Yue De, honorary official for righteousness” [?]; Mingdao and Mingzhi, both honorary officials for righteousness; and Mingshi. His younger brothers were Minghui, Mingxun, and Mingtang. He married Lady Wang. He placed third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Lei 楊雷, registered in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Qiqian; he ranked first in family order, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the seventeenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather Shun, his father Ang, and his mother Lady Jie. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Ting, Ji, Lin, and Yun. He married Lady Xu and subsequently Lady Lu. He placed fifty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and three hundred eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ying 王瑛, registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruyu; he ranked third in family order, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hui, his grandfather Cheng, and his father Pu; his mother was Lady Shao and his stepmother Lady Cheng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Zan and Huan, and his younger brothers Kun, Ling, Long, and Xu. He married Lady Han. He placed thirty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Wei 錢薇, registered in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Maoyuan; he ranked fourteenth in family order, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the twenty-third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shi; his grandfather Da was posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice. His father Zhen was granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under the applicable regulations, and his mother was Lady Zheng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yong, Yue, Zhu, Fen, Jie (a National University student), Lan, Qin, and Xun 壎; his younger brothers were Xuan, Xun 塤, and Kui. He married Lady Sun. He placed thirty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
劉廷範〔貫江西撫州府臨川縣，民籍，儒士，治詩經，字汝顏，行一，年四十，六月三十日生〕。曾祖景昻，祖夢龍，父俸，母甘氏。具慶下，弟廷約、廷功、廷辨，娶葉氏。江西鄉試第七十四名，會試第一百六十五名。

周采〔貫湖廣長沙府寧鄉縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字子亮，行七，年二十六，十二月初六日生〕。曾祖添裕，祖鎮，父策〔知縣〕，母唐氏。重慶下，弟相、檄、榦，娶胡氏。湖廣鄉試第二名，會試第三百九名。

王梃〔貫浙江寧波府象山縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字子長，行三十五，年四十，九月初二日生〕。曾祖在明〔知縣〕，祖京〔推官〕，父渙〔監察御史〕，母周氏。永感下，兄林、桓、樌、檄、楷〔訓導〕、模〔訓術〕、橋、桯、欑，弟棟、極、樀、楊，娶吳氏。浙江鄉試第十六名，會試第六名。

廖天明〔貫江西南昌府奉新縣，軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字敬之，行十七，年四十四，四月二十四日生〕。曾祖彤〔助教〕，祖仕耕，父進，母喻氏，繼母涂氏。具慶下，兄天德，弟天祐，娶梁氏。江西鄉試第五十七名，會試第二百七十五名。
translation_en:
Liu Tingfan 劉廷範 was registered in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Ruyan and ranked first among his brothers; he was forty years old, born on the thirtieth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing'ang; his grandfather, Menglong; his father, Feng; and his mother, née Gan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tingyue, Tinggong, and Tingbian, and his wife was née Ye. He placed seventy-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 165th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Cai 周采 was registered in Ningxiang County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Ziliang and ranked seventh among his brothers; he was twenty-six years old, born on the sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tianyu; his grandfather, Zhen; his father, Ce, a County Magistrate; and his mother, née Tang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Xiang, Xi, and Gan, and his wife was née Hu. He placed second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 309th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ting 王梃 was registered in Xiangshan County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A county government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Zichang and ranked thirty-fifth among his brothers; he was forty years old, born on the second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zaiming, a County Magistrate; his grandfather, Jing, a Prefectural Judge; his father, Huan, an Investigating Censor; and his mother, née Zhou. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Lin, Huan, Guan, Xi, Kai, an Assistant Instructor, Mo, an Instructor in the county School of Yin-yang Studies, Qiao, Ting, and Cuan; his younger brothers were Dong, Ji, Di, and Yang. His wife was née Wu. He placed sixteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liao Tianming 廖天明 was registered in Fengxin County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a military household. A county government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Jingzhi and ranked seventeenth among his brothers; he was forty-four years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong, an Instructor; his grandfather, Shigeng; his father, Jin; his mother, née Yu; and his stepmother, née Tu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tiande, his younger brother was Tianyou, and his wife was née Liang. He placed fifty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cai Runan, registered in an official household in Deqing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zimu; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was eighteen sui old, born on the sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ben, his grandfather Qi (麒), and his father Qi (玘), a tribute student; his mother was née Chen, and his birth mother née Shen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ruzhen, Ruzhou, and Rumei, and his younger brothers Ruyan, Ruli, and Ruming. He married a woman née Zang. He placed thirty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang E, registered in a military household of Sizhou Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region and a native of Wuhu County, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhifu; he ranked first among his brothers and was forty-seven sui old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Zong, his father Ming, and his mother née Zhang. His mother alone was living. His younger brother was Peng, and he married a woman née Jian. He placed 108th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Shu, registered in a military household in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Xingzhi; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-nine sui old, born on the fifteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Rong, a tribute student, his father Gao, a prefectural judge, and his mother née Ye. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Zhong and his younger brother En; he married a woman née Weng. He placed fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 215th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Bangfu, registered in a civilian household in Dingtao County, Cao Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zizhong; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty sui old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Gang, his father Liangguang, and his mother née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiangqing, Luan, and Feng; he married a woman née Chen. He placed fiftieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

羅大用〔貫廣西桂林右衛官籍，湖廣雲夢縣人，國子生，治春秋，字時行，行一，年三十二，八月初一日生〕。曾祖迪〔正千戶〕，祖琮〔指揮同知〕，父衮〔指揮同知〕，母朱氏。具慶下，弟大周、大同，娶朱氏。廣西鄉試第四十二名，會試第二百八十四名。

王梅〔貫浙江嘉興府平湖縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治書經，字時魁，行三，年三十三，二月二十四日生〕。曾祖洪，祖鼎，父鸞，母胡氏，繼母金氏。具慶下，兄桂、槐，弟模、校、森、樞，娶張氏。浙江鄉試第七名，會試第一百二十五名。

王玉汝〔貫廣東廣州府東莞縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字體成，行二，年四十五，九月十六日生〕。曾祖純，祖貞，父尚學〔府同知，進階朝列大夫〕，母梁氏。具慶下，兄士鵬，弟士鸞、用汝、士鳳、士鸘、與汝，娶鄧氏。廣東鄉試第三十四名，會試第二百八名。
translation_en:
Zhu Mo 朱默, courtesy name Shiyan, was registered in a military household of Taicang Guard in Zhili; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twelfth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Lin, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Yue; his father was Xing; and his mother was née Pan. Both parents were living, and his wife was née Xu. He ranked ninety-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Dayong 羅大用, courtesy name Shixing, was registered in an officer household of Guilin Right Guard in Guangxi and was a native of Yunmeng County, Huguang; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the first day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Di, a Battalion Commander; his grandfather was Cong, a Vice Commander; his father was Gun, also a Vice Commander; and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Dazhou and Datong, and his wife was née Zhu. He ranked forty-second in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Mei 王梅, courtesy name Shikui, was registered in a civilian household of Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang; he was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, third in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Hong; his grandfather was Ding; his father was Luan; his mother was née Hu; and his stepmother was née Jin. Both parents were living; his elder brothers were Gui and Huai, his younger brothers were Mo, Xiao, Sen, and Shu, and his wife was née Zhang. He ranked seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yuru 王玉汝, courtesy name Ticheng, was registered in a military household of Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, second in birth order, aged forty-five, and born on the sixteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Chun; his grandfather was Zhen; his father was Shangxue, a Vice Prefect promoted in rank to Grand Master of Court Rank (chaolie dafu); and his mother was née Liang. Both parents were living; his elder brother was Shipeng, his younger brothers were Shiluan, Yongru, Shifeng, Shishuang, and Yuru 與汝, and his wife was née Deng. He ranked thirty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.
